patent_details: The compound 4-(4-formyl-2-thiazolyl)-1-[2-[5-methyl-3-(trifluoromethyl)-1H-pyrazole-1-yl]acetyl]piperidine (220 mg) and 3-fluoro-6-methylsulfonyloxy-1,2-benzenedimethanol (150 mg) and para-toluenesulfonic acid monohydrate (20 mg) were dissolved in toluene (15 mL), then reacted and purified similarly to the preparation of Compound 1-3 to obtain the subject compound as a white amorphous solid (297 mg, yield 84%). full_recipe.reaction_name: HATU/DIPEA-mediated amide coupling of a piperidinium chloride with a pyrazolylacetic acid

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High plausibility / recommended with minor optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a standard tertiary amide formation between the piperidinium chloride amine precursor and the carboxylic acid. HATU/DIPEA in DMF is appropriate. The key optimization is to use enough DIPEA to neutralize the amine hydrochloride and the carboxylic acid and to promote coupling. The aryl mesylate and acetal-like benzodioxane motif should be compatible under these mild, anhydrous, room-temperature conditions. No single-step retrosynthetic alternative is clearly superior, although COMU, T3P, or EDCI/Oxyma could be alternatives.

solvents.name: DMF
solvents.volume: 5-10 mL per mmol of limiting amine substrate

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve the piperidinium chloride amine precursor, 1.0 equiv, and the substituted pyrazolylacetic acid, 1.05 equiv, in anhydrous DMF at approximately 0.1-0.2 M concentration. Cool to 0 °C if exotherm control is desired, then add DIPEA, 3.0 equiv, followed by HATU, 1.15 equiv. Stir at 0 °C for 15-30 min, then allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 12-16 h. Monitor by LCMS or HPLC for consumption of the amine. Upon completion, dilute with ethyl acetate or another suitable organic solvent and wash sequentially with water, saturated sodium bicarbonate, water, and brine. Dry the organic layer over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by flash chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the target amide: Cc1cc(C(F)(F)F)nn1CC(=O)N1CCC(c2nc(C3OCc4c(F)ccc(OS(C)(=O)=O)c4CO3)cs2)CC1.

full_recipe.reaction_name: N-sulfonylation of an aryl amine with 3-methylbenzenesulfonyl chloride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High plausibility; recommended with minor optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The pathway is a standard sulfonamide formation from an aniline-type aryl amine using an arylsulfonyl chloride. Pyridine is suitable as both solvent and HCl scavenger. The tertiary amine in the substrate may become protonated during the reaction, so using excess pyridine and slight excess sulfonyl chloride is appropriate. The reaction is chemically plausible and likely selective for the aniline NH2 group. Recommended optimization: add sulfonyl chloride at 0 °C, then warm to room temperature; use 1.1–1.3 equiv sulfonyl chloride and pyridine as solvent/base.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve the aryl amine substrate, CCCCCCN1CC[C@@](C)(c2cccc(N)c2)[C@H](C)C1, in dry pyridine at about 0.1 M concentration, using approximately 10 mL pyridine per 1 mmol substrate. Cool the solution to 0 °C. Add 3-methylbenzenesulfonyl chloride, Cc1cccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)c1, portionwise or dropwise, using 1.2 equivalents. Stir at 0 °C for 30–60 min, then allow the mixture to warm to 20–25 °C and stir for 12–18 h. Monitor by LCMS or TLC until consumption of starting aniline. Quench by adding water or saturated aqueous NaHCO3 slowly at 0–25 °C. Extract with ethyl acetate or dichloromethane. Wash the organic layer with dilute aqueous acid to remove pyridine if compatible, then with saturated NaHCO3 and brine. Dry over Na2SO4, filter, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford CCCCCCN1CC[C@@](C)(c2cccc(NS(=O)(=O)c3cccc(C)c3)c2)[C@H](C)C1.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Single-step aryl amide formation via HATU-mediated coupling

recommendation_and_ranking.overall_assessment: The proposed transformation is a plausible single-step amide coupling between a substituted benzoic acid and an electron-poor aryl amine. The given EDC/HOBt/Et3N/DMF recipe should work, but it is not optimal because the aminocarbazole/aniline nucleophile is relatively weak and sterically demanding. A stronger uronium coupling system such as HATU/DIPEA in dry DMF is recommended.

ranking.rationale: Best choice for coupling a hindered/electron-poor aryl amine to a benzoic acid. Faster activation and generally higher conversion than EDC/HOBt.
Chemically plausible and likely to give product, but may be slow or incomplete with this aryl amine. HOBt also has handling concerns when dry.

ranking.recipe: Acid chloride formation followed by amine addition
ranking.rationale: Possible but less selective and harsher; risk of decomposition or side reactions with the pivalamide/heteroaryl substrate.

recommendation_and_ranking.recommended_pathway: Use the same initial reactants, but replace EDC/HOBt/Et3N with HATU/DIPEA for a more robust single-step retrosynthetic recipe.

procedure: Dry a reaction flask and maintain under nitrogen or argon.
Charge the flask with the substituted chlorobenzoic acid intermediate, aminocarbazole amine, and dry DMF to give about 0.1 M concentration.
Add DIPEA, then add HATU portionwise at room temperature.
Stir at room temperature for 15–30 min, then heat to 45 °C for 16 h.
Monitor by LC-MS or HPLC for consumption of the aminocarbazole amine.
After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and wash with water, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine.
Dry the organic layer over sodium sulfate, filter, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the target amide product.

patent_details: To a reaction flask was added 1-ethylpiperazine (1.8 g, 16 mmol), 6-bromo-pyridine-3-carboxaldehyde (3 g, 16 mmol) and dichloromethane (50 mL), and sodium triacetoxyborohydride (3.7 g, 17.5 mmol) was added in portions under stirring. The mixture was stirred at room temperature for 12 hours to give rise to a reaction. To the reaction liquid were added dichloromethane (20 mL) and aqueous sodium hydroxide solution (2N, 15 mL). The aqueous phase was extracted with dichloromethane (20 mL×2) and the phases were separated. The organic phases were combined, washed with saturated sodium chloride solution (20 mL×2), dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate and filtered with suction. The filtrate was concentrated under reduced pressure to give the title compound as a yellow oil (3.6 g, yield 80%).   MS m/z (ESI): 285.2 (M+H)

full_recipe.reaction_name: N-alkylation of 1-ethylpiperazine with bromomethyl-bromopyridine via SN2 substitution

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High / Rank 1: plausible and recommended with minor optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The pathway is chemically sound: the secondary amine of 1-ethylpiperazine reacts with the benzylic/heteroarylmethyl bromide by SN2 alkylation to give the tertiary amine product. K2CO3 in acetonitrile is a standard mild basic system for this transformation. Main risks are quaternization if excess alkyl bromide is used, hydrolysis/decomposition of the bromomethyl heteroarene, and incomplete conversion at room temperature. Use slight excess 1-ethylpiperazine and controlled heating.

procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry flask with bromomethyl-bromopyridine, 1-ethylpiperazine, and dry acetonitrile.
Add finely powdered anhydrous potassium carbonate portionwise with stirring.
Heat at 60 °C for about 12 h and monitor by LCMS or TLC until the alkyl bromide is consumed.
Cool to room temperature, filter off inorganic salts, and rinse the solids with acetonitrile or ethyl acetate.
Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure.
Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol with 0.5–1% triethylamine or by acid-base extraction to obtain CCN1CCN(Cc2ccc(Br)nc2)CC1.
Recommendation: avoid excess bromomethyl-bromopyridine to minimize tertiary amine quaternization; a slight excess of 1-ethylpiperazine is preferred.

patent_details: To a solution of 3-[6-(ethylthio)-3,4,8,9-tetrahydro-3,3,8,8-tetramethylfuro[2,3-h]isoquinolin-1-yl]benzoic acid (1.76 g, 4.30 mmol), α,α-dimethylglycine amide hydrochloride (655 mg, 4.73 mmol), 1-hydroxy-1H-benzotriazole monohydrate (724 mg, 4.73 mmol) and triethylamine (1.50 ml, 10.8 mmol) in N,N-dimethylformamide (8 ml) was added 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide hydrochloride (1.07 g, 5.59 mmol) under ice-cooling, and the mixture was stirred at room temperature for 15 hours. full_recipe.reaction_name: Single-step amide coupling of a sterically hindered benzoic acid with 2-amino-2-methylpropanamide

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended with optimization; original EDC/HOBt/Et3N/DMF recipe ranked 3/5, optimized HATU/DIPEA/DMF recipe ranked 4/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is a straightforward carboxylic acid to amide coupling between the aryl carboxylic acid and the primary amino group of 2-amino-2-methylpropanamide. The original EDC/HOBt/triethylamine conditions are chemically plausible, but the substrate is bulky and the aminoamide may be poorly soluble or partially protonated, so conversion may be moderate. A uronium coupling reagent such as HATU with DIPEA in dry DMF is likely more reliable for this hindered acid and amine combination. Use slight excess aminoamide and base to suppress incomplete conversion.

solvents.name: N,N-dimethylformamide
solvents.volume: 10 mL per 1 mmol aryl carboxylic acid

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the aryl carboxylic acid substrate in dry DMF using about 10 mL per mmol of acid. Cool to 0 °C. Add HATU, followed by DIPEA, and stir for 10–15 minutes to pre-activate the acid. Add 2-amino-2-methylpropanamide in one portion or as a DMF solution. Allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C and stir for 16 hours. Monitor by LCMS or HPLC for disappearance of the acid. After completion, dilute with ethyl acetate and wash with water, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine. Dry the organic phase over sodium sulfate, filter, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the target amide product.

patent_details: Tert-butyl (S)-2-(piperazin-1-carbonyl)pyrrolidin-1-carboxylate (0.283 g, 1.000 mmol) prepared in step 1 of example 64, propan-2-sulfonyl chloride (0.226 mL, 2.000 mmol) and potassium carbonate (0.415 g, 3.000 mmol) were dissolved in acetonitrile (8 mL) at room temperature, after which the resulting solution was stirred at 50°C. for 18 hours, and then a reaction was finished by lowering the temperature to room temperature. Water was poured into the reaction mixture, and then an organic layer was extracted with dichloromethane, filtered via a plastic filter to remove a solid residue and an aqueous solution layer therefrom, and concentrated under reduced pressure. An obtained product was used without an additional purification process (title compound, 0.770 g, 98.8%, light yellow oil).

full_recipe.reaction_name: HATU-mediated amide coupling of N-Boc-proline with 1-(propan-2-ylsulfonyl)piperazine

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 1/1 - recommended single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The target product is the direct amide-coupling product of N-Boc-proline carboxylic acid and the free secondary amine of 1-(propan-2-ylsulfonyl)piperazine. HATU/base in DMF is a highly plausible and standard recipe for this transformation. The listed chloride likely represents an amine HCl salt, so sufficient base is required to liberate the amine and neutralize acid generated during activation. Stereochemical integrity should be largely retained if the reaction is started cold and not over-heated. Minor optimization: DIPEA is often preferred over triethylamine, but triethylamine at higher equivalents is acceptable.

reactants.name: 1-(propan-2-ylsulfonyl)piperazine hydrochloride or chloride salt
reactants.quantity_for_scale: 1.10 mmol, approximately 252 mg if HCl salt

procedure: Charge a dry nitrogen-flushed flask with N-Boc-proline acid and 1-(propan-2-ylsulfonyl)piperazine hydrochloride or chloride salt.
Add dry DMF to give approximately 0.10 M concentration with respect to the acid.
Cool the mixture to 0 °C and add triethylamine slowly. Stir for 5-10 minutes to liberate the free amine if an HCl salt is used.
Add HATU portionwise at 0 °C, then allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C.
Stir for approximately 16 hours and monitor by LCMS or HPLC until the acid is consumed.
Dilute with ethyl acetate, wash successively with water, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine.
Dry the organic layer over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate.
Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the Boc-prolyl piperazine sulfonamide product.

patent_details: In a round-bottom flask with a nitrogen atmosphere and containing a mechanical stirrer, a thermometer and an addition funnel, was combined 1,073 grams (10.9 moles) of maleic anhydride (commercially available from Aldrich Chemical, Milwaukee, Wis.) and 6,062 grams of acetonitrile. The mixture was stirred to dissolve the solids and cooled to −7°C. To this was slowly added 800 grams, (10.9 moles) of tert-butylamine (commercially available from Aldrich Chemical, Milwaukee, Wis.) at a rate such that the temperature remained below 0°C. (approximately 2.5 hour addition time). The mixture was stirred at −7°C. for one hour and then overnight at room temperature. The solid was collected by filtration, washed with 500 milliliters acetonitrile and dried to give 1,355 grams of (Z)-4-(tert-butylamino)-4-oxo-2-butenoic acid as a white solid.¹³C NMR indicated the product to be 94.62 weight % (Z)-4-(tert-butylamino)-4-oxo-2-butenoic acid, and 5.38 weight % tert-butylamine. This material was used without further purification for the next reaction.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Ring-opening aminolysis of maleic anhydride to N-tert-butylmaleamic acid

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High; ranked 1/1 for this single-step disconnection
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The pathway is chemically plausible and direct: tert-butylamine opens maleic anhydride to give the corresponding monoamide-monoacid. The proposed triethylamine/toluene recipe is workable but not optimal because triethylamine is not required and may form the triethylammonium carboxylate salt, complicating isolation of the free acid. Toluene is acceptable if product precipitation is desired, but THF or ethyl acetate often gives better mixing. Best optimization is slow addition of tert-butylamine at 0–5 °C, then warm to room temperature, avoiding heat to minimize dehydration to N-tert-butylmaleimide.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 10 mmol scale, charge a dry flask with maleic anhydride, add dry toluene to give about 0.2 M concentration, and cool to 0–5 °C under nitrogen. Add tert-butylamine slowly over 15–30 min while maintaining the temperature below 10 °C. After addition, allow the mixture to warm to 20–25 °C and stir for about 3 h. Monitor consumption of maleic anhydride by TLC, LCMS, or NMR. The product often precipitates; collect by filtration, wash with cold toluene or hexane, and dry under vacuum. If triethylamine was used in the original recipe, avoid using stoichiometric amounts; omit it for the free acid product, or use only catalytic/trace amounts if solubility issues require it. Avoid heating because it can promote dehydration/cyclization to the maleimide.

patent_details: Triethylamine (26 mL, 186.5 mmol) was added dropwise to a cooled (0°C.) solution of (1R,4R)-4,7,7-trimethyl-3-oxo-bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane-2-carbonyl chloride (Intermediate 20; 13.33 g, 62.1 mmol) in dichloromethane (150 mL), yielding a thick suspension. This was stirred for 3 min and then N′-(2,5-dichloro-phenyl)-hydrazinecarboxylic acid tert-butyl ester (Intermediate 34; 13.00 g, 46.9 mmol) was added in one portion. The cooling bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature for 10 min, then in an oil-bath at 50°C. for 4 h. The reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature, then added to water (200 mL) and extracted with dichloromethane (3×150 mL). The combined organic layers were washed with brine (200 mL), dried ( magnesium sulfate), filtered, and evaporated to give N′-(2,5-dichloro-phenyl)-N′-((1R,4R)-4,7,7-trimethyl-3-oxo-bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane-2-carbonyl)-hydrazinecarboxylic acid tert-butyl ester (29.55 g, 138% of the expected amount) as a brown oil. This was used directly in the next step without further purification.

full_recipe.reaction_name: N-acylation of Boc-protected arylhydrazine with a bicyclic keto acid chloride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High plausibility; recommended single-step route, rank 1/1
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a standard hydrazine N-acylation using an acid chloride and triethylamine. The desired product is formed by acylation of the more nucleophilic aryl-substituted hydrazine nitrogen of the Boc-protected hydrazine. The route is chemically plausible and concise. Main risks are acid chloride hydrolysis, competing minor acylation at the Boc-protected nitrogen, and base-promoted epimerization/enolization of the keto acid chloride. These are minimized by dry solvent, inert atmosphere, low-temperature addition, and mild base.

procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve tert-butyl 2-(2,5-dichlorophenyl)hydrazine-1-carboxylate, 1.0 equiv, in anhydrous dichloromethane at about 0.1 M concentration.
Add triethylamine, 2.0 equiv, and cool the mixture to 0 °C.
Prepare a separate solution of the bicyclic keto acid chloride, 1.05 equiv, in a small portion of anhydrous dichloromethane.
Add the acid chloride solution dropwise at 0 °C over about 15 minutes.
Stir at 0 °C for 30 minutes, then allow the mixture to warm to 20 °C and stir for about 2.5–3 hours, monitoring by TLC or LC-MS.
After completion, dilute with dichloromethane and wash sequentially with water, dilute aqueous acid to remove triethylamine, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine.
Dry the organic phase over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
Purify the crude product by flash chromatography using an appropriate hexane/ethyl acetate gradient to afford the desired Boc-protected N-acyl arylhydrazine.

full_recipe.reaction_name: SNAr amination of activated heteroaryl fluoride with 2-(morpholin-4-yl)ethylamine

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good pathway, but original conditions are suboptimal; recommended rank: 3.5/5 for the submitted recipe, 4.5/5 after optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is chemically plausible: the heteroaryl fluoride is strongly activated toward nucleophilic aromatic substitution by multiple ring nitrogens and a cyano substituent, and 2-(morpholin-4-yl)ethylamine is an appropriate nucleophile. However, triethylamine in dichloromethane is likely too mild/low-boiling for efficient displacement of aryl fluoride. A polar aprotic solvent and elevated temperature are recommended. The same single-step retrosynthesis is retained: target product from the fluoro precursor plus 2-(morpholin-4-yl)ethylamine.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry sealed tube or Schlenk flask with the activated heteroaryl fluoride precursor, 2-(morpholin-4-yl)ethylamine, and anhydrous N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone. Add N,N-diisopropylethylamine, seal, and heat at 100 °C for 12 h with stirring. Monitor conversion by LC-MS or HPLC. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and wash with water followed by brine. Dry the organic layer over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol with a small amount of ammonium hydroxide or by preparative HPLC to afford the desired SNAr amination product.

patent_details: To a suspension of 9-chloro-3-methyl-5-piperidin-3-yl-5H-isoxazolo[4,3-c]quinolin-4-one hydroiodide (50 mg, 0.11 mmol) in tetrahydrofuran (3 mL) add benzyl isocyanate (16 μL, 0.12 mmol) and follow by potassium carbonate (23 mg, 0.17). Stir the mixture at room temperature under nitrogen overnight. concentrate the mixture, partition between 20% isopropanol/chloroform and water, and separate. Wash the organic layer with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate solution, brine, dry over magnesium sulfate and concentrate. Purify by flash chromatography on silica gel (eluting with 0-0.5% methanol/chloroform) to give 44.4 mg of the title compound as an orange solid, 88% yield.¹H NMR: consistent with structure. MS (ion spray) 451 (M⁺).

full_recipe.reaction_name: Secondary amine benzyl-isocyanate addition / unsymmetrical urea formation

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Rank 1: plausible and recommended with minor optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The pathway is chemically sound: the secondary piperidine nitrogen in the starting heteroaryl lactam reacts directly with benzyl isocyanate to form the target N-benzyl urea. Triethylamine is useful if the amine is present as a hydroiodide/acid salt; otherwise it is not essential. The listed solvent SMILES ClCCl corresponds to dichloromethane, which is appropriate. The only concern is the ambiguous '.I' in the reactants: if it means hydroiodide salt, use excess base; if it means elemental iodine, it should be omitted.

reactants.name: piperidinyl heteroaryl lactam amine, preferably free base; if isolated as HI salt, use as listed
reactants.quantity_recommendation: 1.00 mmol scale; exact mass depends on salt/free-base form

reagents.name: triethylamine
reagents.quantity_recommendation: 2.20 mmol per 1.00 mmol amine; reduce to 0-0.2 equiv if using free-base amine

full_recipe.procedure: Under dry nitrogen, dissolve or suspend the starting piperidinyl heteroaryl lactam amine, 1.00 equiv, in anhydrous dichloromethane at about 0.1 M. Add triethylamine, 2.2 equiv, especially if the starting material is a hydroiodide salt, and stir for 5-10 min at 20-25 °C. Add benzyl isocyanate, 1.1 equiv, dropwise at room temperature. Stir at 25 °C for about 4 h and monitor by LCMS or HPLC until the amine is consumed. Quench with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride or water, separate the layers, wash the organic phase with brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to obtain the target urea product. Avoid moisture and handle benzyl isocyanate in a well-ventilated fume hood.

patent_details: Preparation of 2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-malonic acid dimethyl ester (54): To a solution of anhydrous methanol (250 mL) is added sodium metal (2.875 g, 0.125 mol) piecewise until the evolution of gas has deceased. Dimethyl malonate (16.5 g, 0.125 mol) is added dropwise and the mixture is stirred for 30 minutes. 4-Fluoro benzyl bromide (23.8 g, 0.126 mol) is added dropwise, and the reaction is refluxed for 2 hour. The majority of the solvent is removed under vacuum, and aqueous HCl is added. The solution is extracted with CHCl₃, dried, and the solvent removed in vacuo. Distillation of the crude material under reduced pressure provides the desired compound which is used without further purification.   Preparation of 2-(4-fluorobenxyl)-malonic acid benzyl ester methyl ester (55): Lipozyme (4.0 g) is added to a solution of 2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-malonic acid dimethyl ester, 54, (1.0, 4.7 mmol) and benzyl alcohol (2.9 mL) in hexane (30 mL). The suspension is shaken at 40°C. and 200 rpm. After 18 hours the reaction is filtered, the solvent is removed in vacuo and the crude product purified over silica to afford the desired product which is used without further purification.   Preparation of 2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-malonic acid monomethyl ester (56): 5% Pd/C (64 mg) is added to a solution of 2-(4-fluorobenxyl)-malonic acid benzyl ester methyl ester, 55, (126 mg, 0.4 mmol) in 1:1 hexane/toluene (20 mL). Hydrogenation is carried out at RT until starting material is consumed. The catalyst is removed by filtration, and the solvent removed in vacuo to afford the desired product which is used without further purification.   Preparation of 3-(4-cylcohexyl-4-[1,2,4]triazol-1-ylmethyl-piperidin-1-yl)-2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-3-oxo-propionic acid methyl ester (57): To a solution of 2-(4-fluoro-benzyl)-malonic acid monomethyl ester, 56, (47.5 mg, 0.21 mmol), 4-cyclohexyl-4-[1,2,4]triazol-1-ylmethyl-piperidine, 18, (50 mg, 0.20 mmol), 1-hydroxybenzotriazole (54 mg, 0.40 mmol), 4-methylmorpholine (88 □l, 0.80 mmol) in N,N-dimethylformamide (7 mL) is added 1-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)-3-ethylcarbodiimide (50 mg, 0.26 mmol). The reaction mixture is stirred overnight and then aqueous ammonium chloride is added. full_recipe.reaction_name: Base-promoted SNAr N-arylation of a secondary piperazine with a chloro-heteroaryl thiadiazole

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / plausible, but not fully optimal
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a plausible nucleophilic aromatic substitution: the secondary piperazine nitrogen attacks the electron-poor chloro-thiadiazole to give the N-heteroaryl piperazine product. DMF is an appropriate polar aprotic solvent and triethylamine can neutralize generated HCl. However, the presence of trifluoroacetic acid is counterproductive unless the piperazine substrate is being used as its TFA salt; it will protonate the nucleophilic amine and slow the reaction. The optimized single-step recommendation is to use the free-base piperazine when possible, omit TFA, and use excess triethylamine or preferably DIPEA/K2CO3 with heating.

full_recipe.reaction_name: O-carbamoylation of hydroxypyridine with N-methyl-N-phenylcarbamoyl chloride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended with minor optimization; Rank: 2/3
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is chemically plausible: the hydroxypyridine/phenol substrate can react with N-methyl-N-phenylcarbamoyl chloride to give the desired O-carbamate. full_recipe.reaction_name: BBr3-mediated O-debenzylation of an aryl benzyl ether to phenol

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended, Rank 1 for a non-reductive single-step route; overall 4/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is chemically plausible: BBr3 in anhydrous dichloromethane is a standard reagent system for cleaving aryl benzyl ethers to phenols. The recipe should be run cold and anhydrous because BBr3 is harsh and can potentially affect the ethyl carbamate or other Lewis-basic/carbonyl sites. The original recipe is incomplete because it lacks temperature, stoichiometry, time, and quench details. Optimized conditions are recommended below. A Pd/C hydrogenolysis alternative could be considered, but this substrate contains a conjugated heteroaryl ketone system that may be sensitive to reduction, so BBr3 is a reasonable choice.

reagents.name: boron tribromide, 1.0 M solution in dichloromethane
saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate, workup quench

procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve the benzyl-protected substrate in anhydrous dichloromethane at approximately 0.10 M concentration.
Cool the solution to -78 °C.
Add 1.5 equivalents of 1.0 M BBr3 in dichloromethane dropwise while maintaining -78 °C.
Stir at -78 °C for 1 hour, then allow the mixture to warm slowly to room temperature over about 3 hours.
Monitor by LC-MS or TLC. If starting material remains, cool again and add up to 0.5 equivalent additional BBr3.
After completion, cool to -78 °C and carefully quench dropwise with methanol.
Allow to warm to room temperature, then add saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate slowly until gas evolution ceases and the mixture is near neutral.
Extract with dichloromethane or ethyl acetate, wash the organic layer with brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate.
Purify by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol or ethyl acetate/hexanes as appropriate to give the phenol product: CCOC(=O)N1CCC(c2oc3c(C)c(O)ccc3c(=O)c2C)CC1.

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High plausibility; ranked 1st among simple one-step retrosynthetic options for this target
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The starting malononitrile derivative has one acidic methine proton between two nitriles. NaH can cleanly generate the carbanion, which should undergo SN2 alkylation with primary 1-iodo-3-fluoropropane to give the desired quaternary malononitrile. The pathway is chemically reasonable. Main risks are over-basic conditions, competing elimination of the alkyl iodide, and safety issues using NaH in DMF, so the reaction should be run cold-to-room-temperature under inert atmosphere and not heated.

Allow the mixture to warm to 20–25 °C and stir for about 12 h, monitoring by LC-MS, GC-MS, or NMR. When complete, cool to 0 °C and carefully quench residual hydride with saturated NH4Cl solution added slowly. full_recipe.reaction_name: Knochel iodine-magnesium exchange followed by heteroaryl aldehyde addition

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good/Recommended with modification: 4/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The proposed disconnection is plausible: selective I/Mg exchange on the heteroaryl iodide should generate the heteroaryl magnesium species, which can add to the heteroaryl aldehyde to give the racemic secondary alcohol. procedure: Dry the flask, maintain nitrogen or argon atmosphere, and use anhydrous THF.

Cool the organomagnesium solution to -78 °C.
Add a THF solution of CSc1ncc(C=O)cn1 slowly at -78 °C. Keep the aldehyde separate until this step.
Stir 0.5 h at -78 °C, then allow the reaction to warm gradually to 0 °C over about 2 h.
Quench carefully with saturated aqueous NH4Cl at 0 °C, extract with ethyl acetate or dichloromethane, wash, dry, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC.

recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The proposed disconnection is correct: the product is formed by N-benzylation through reductive amination of the aldehyde with the secondary cyclic amine. Sodium triacetoxyborohydride in dichloromethane is a standard, mild, chemoselective reagent system for aldehyde reductive amination and is compatible with phenol, anisole, and indoline motifs. The original recipe is plausible; optimization is to run dry, add a small amount of acetic acid, and use slight excess amine and 1.5 equiv NaBH(OAc)3. Add sodium triacetoxyborohydride portionwise, 1.5 equiv, keeping the mixture near room temperature. Stir at 25 °C for about 16 h and monitor disappearance of aldehyde by TLC or LCMS. Quench carefully with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate, separate layers, extract the aqueous phase with dichloromethane, dry the combined organic layers, filter, and concentrate. recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 1 = recommended/acceptable but monitor closely; 2 = Buchwald-Hartwig Pd coupling as backup; 3 = SNAr/displacement approaches not recommended
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The proposed transformation is chemically plausible: an electron-poor aryl iodide bearing a sulfonamide is coupled with a weakly nucleophilic 2-amino-1,3,4-thiadiazole. The listed CuI/1,10-phenanthroline/Cs2CO3/DMF system is a standard Ullmann-type N-arylation recipe and should be viable. Main risks are low conversion due to the weak heteroaryl amine, catalyst/base inhibition by the sulfonamide/thiazole nitrogens, and possible competing N-arylation of the sulfonamide. Monitor by LCMS or HPLC; if aryl iodide remains, continue up to 24 h or add an extra 0.05 equiv CuI and 0.1 equiv phenanthroline. Cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, filter through Celite to remove inorganic solids and copper residues, and wash with water and brine. recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The target transformation is a direct replacement of aryl bromide by morpholine, consistent with CuI/N,N-dimethylglycine/K2CO3 Ullmann amination. The pathway is chemically plausible, but the original recipe is not optimal because ethyl acetate is a poor high-temperature Ullmann solvent and HCl/Cl would protonate morpholine and reduce nucleophilicity. Cool to room temperature, dilute with water, and extract with ethyl acetate. Wash organic layers with water and brine to remove DMSO, dry over Na2SO4, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to give the aryl morpholine product. Avoid adding HCl in the coupling step.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Single-step N-acylation of methyl L-serinate hydrochloride by carbodiimide-mediated amide coupling

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Plausible; recommended with minor optimization. Rank: 2/3 as written, 1/3 if HOBt is replaced by Oxyma or if fresh wet HOBt is used carefully.
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is a standard amide coupling between a carboxylic acid and methyl serinate hydrochloride. EDC·HCl/HOBt with triethylamine in dichloromethane can form the desired amide. The free serine alcohol is unlikely to dominate over N-acylation, but some O-acylation or esterification side products are possible. The amine is present as HCl salt, so sufficient base is required. The stereochemical change from [C@@H] in the amino ester to [C@H] in the product is likely a CIP-priority descriptor change after N-acylation, not true inversion; retention is expected. Main concerns are HOBt safety, limited solubility in DCM, and possible racemization if warmed too long or overbased. A safer/cleaner optimized single-step route uses EDC·HCl/Oxyma or HATU/DIPEA in DCM/DMF.

reagents.name: Oxyma Pure, preferred safer additive instead of HOBt

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, suspend or dissolve the carboxylic acid and Oxyma in dichloromethane with optional DMF. Cool to 0 °C. Add EDC·HCl, then add DIPEA slowly. Stir 10-20 min at 0 °C to preactivate. Add methyl L-serinate hydrochloride portionwise, followed by the remaining DIPEA if needed to maintain basic conditions. Warm to 20-25 °C and stir 12-18 h while monitoring by LCMS or HPLC. Quench with water, dilute with dichloromethane or ethyl acetate, wash sequentially with dilute acid, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine. Dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to give methyl N-acyl-L-serinate. If the original recipe must be used, use triethylamine 3.0 equivalents, EDC·HCl 1.2 equivalents, and wet HOBt 1.1 equivalents in dichloromethane/DMF at the same temperature profile; avoid dry HOBt due to explosion hazard.

full_recipe.reaction_name: SN2 N-alkylation of piperidine with a primary 3-bromopropyl ether

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 4/5 for the optimized single-step route; 3/5 for the originally stated ethanol/piperidine-only recipe
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is chemically plausible: piperidine can displace bromide from the primary 3-bromopropoxy substrate by SN2 to give the tertiary amine product. The original recipe using piperidine in ethanol should work, but it is not optimal because HBr generated during the reaction can protonate piperidine and slow conversion. Excess piperidine helps, but adding an inorganic base such as K2CO3 and optional KI improves conversion and suppresses formation of the piperidinium bromide salt. Ethanol is acceptable, but acetonitrile or DMF often gives faster SN2 reactions. A practical optimized recipe is substrate + excess piperidine + K2CO3 + catalytic KI in ethanol or acetonitrile at reflux.

Add ethanol at approximately 10 mL per mmol of substrate, then add piperidine. Heat the mixture at reflux, about 78 °C, for 12-18 hours with stirring. Monitor conversion by TLC or LC-MS. After completion, cool to room temperature and filter off inorganic salts. Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure. Partition the residue between ethyl acetate and water, then wash the organic layer with water and brine. Dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to obtain the piperidino-propoxy quinolinone product. If the free base is difficult to isolate, convert to a suitable acid salt after purification.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Single-step SNAr amination of an activated chloro-azaheteroaryl electrophile with 3,4-ethylenedioxyaniline

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended optimized route: Rank 1/3; original toluene/Na2SO4/collidine recipe: Rank 2/3
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The desired C-N bond formation is chemically plausible by nucleophilic aromatic substitution because the heteroaryl chloride is activated by adjacent ring nitrogens. The aniline nucleophile should displace chloride under heat with a non-nucleophilic base to trap HCl. The original recipe is plausible if collidine is acting as base, but Na2SO4 is not a true reagent and toluene is relatively nonpolar/low-boiling, so conversion may be slow or incomplete. A better single-step recipe is to use dry NMP or DMAc with 2,4,6-collidine or DIPEA at 120-130 °C.

procedure: Charge a dry nitrogen-flushed reaction vessel with the chloro-azaheteroaryl electrophile, 3,4-ethylenedioxyaniline, and anhydrous NMP.
Add 2,4,6-collidine as HCl scavenger. Maintain approximately 0.2 M concentration based on the electrophile.
Heat at 125 °C under nitrogen for 12-18 hours, monitoring by LC-MS or HPLC for disappearance of the chloro electrophile.
Cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and wash with water several times to remove NMP and collidine salts.
Wash the organic layer with brine, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate.
Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or trituration/recrystallization to obtain the target anilino azaheteroaryl product.

Note: Sodium sulfate from the original recipe should be used only as a drying agent during workup, not as a reaction reagent. If the optimized SNAr gives poor conversion, a Buchwald-Hartwig amination variant should be evaluated.

full_recipe.reaction_name: HATU/DIPEA-mediated amide coupling of carboxylic acid with cyclohexylamine

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 1 - recommended single-step pathway
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The transformation is a direct conversion of the carboxylic acid to the cyclohexylamide. The proposed reagents correspond to HATU/PF6 with DIPEA and cyclohexylamine, which is a plausible and commonly effective amide-coupling system. The Boc carbamate, secondary alcohol, lactam, aryl fluorides, and tertiary amine/lactam motif should generally tolerate these mild conditions. Main optimization concern is solubility in dichloromethane; adding a small amount of DMF or using DCM/DMF improves robustness. Avoid excess cyclohexylamine and prolonged reaction to minimize side reactions.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the carboxylic acid starting material in dry dichloromethane/DMF at about 0.1 M concentration. Cool to 0 °C if convenient, then add DIPEA followed by HATU. Stir for 10-15 minutes to form the activated ester. Add cyclohexylamine slowly, then allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for about 4 hours, monitoring by LCMS or HPLC. After completion, dilute with dichloromethane and wash sequentially with water, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine. Dry the organic phase over sodium sulfate, filter, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to obtain the cyclohexylamide product.

patent_details: At 0°C., 27.5 g of 2-fluoro-4-methylaniline are initially charged in 300 ml of dichloromethane, 26.7 g of triethylamine are added and 50.8 g of trifluoroacetic anhydride are then added dropwise. full_recipe.reaction_name: N-trifluoroacetylation of 2-fluoro-4-methylaniline with trifluoroacetic anhydride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Rank 1: Recommended after optimization. The given pathway is chemically plausible but suboptimal without an added base.
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is a straightforward aniline acylation to give the corresponding trifluoroacetamide. Trifluoroacetic anhydride is an excellent single-step reagent for this retrosynthesis: product = 2-fluoro-4-methylaniline + trifluoroacetic anhydride. However, the original recipe using only trifluoroacetic anhydride in dichloromethane/dichloroalkane can form trifluoroacetic acid, which protonates the aniline and slows conversion. Adding triethylamine or DIPEA as an acid scavenger makes the reaction cleaner and more reliable. Mild temperature is preferred; heating is unnecessary.

procedure: In a dry flask under nitrogen, dissolve 2-fluoro-4-methylaniline, 1.00 equiv, in dry dichloromethane, about 10 mL per mmol.
Add triethylamine, 1.5 equiv, and cool the mixture to 0 °C.
Add trifluoroacetic anhydride, 1.1 equiv, dropwise while maintaining 0 °C.
After addition, allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C and stir for about 2 hours. Monitor by TLC, LC-MS, or HPLC until the aniline is consumed.
Cool again to 0 °C and carefully quench with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate until gas evolution ceases.
Separate the organic layer, wash with water, dilute aqueous HCl if needed to remove residual amine/triethylamine, then brine.
Dry the organic phase over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate.
Purify by crystallization or flash chromatography if required to obtain Cc1ccc(NC(=O)C(F)(F)F)c(F)c1.

patent_details: To a stirred suspension of 1-(3,4-dichloro-1,2-thiazol-5-yl)-N-hydroxy-1-(3-thienyl)methanimine (1.69 g, 6.06 mmol), 2-(chloromethyl)pyrimidin-4-amine (957 mg, 6.66 mmol) and potassium iodide (1.01 g, 6.06 mmol) in acetonitrile (15 mL) at 0°C. was added 1,5-diazabicyclo(4.3.0)non-5-ene (1.52 mL, 12.7 mmol). full_recipe.reaction_name: TFA-mediated Boc deprotection of heteroaryl carbamate to free amino heteroaryl product

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High / Rank 1 for this single-step transformation
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The reactant is a Boc-protected amino heteroaryl compound, and the product is the corresponding free amine. Trifluoroacetic acid in dichloromethane is a standard and generally effective condition for Boc removal. The pathway is chemically plausible and likely to work. The main caution is that the substrate contains an oxime ether-like N-O-C=N motif and multiple heteroaryl chlorides, so prolonged strong acid exposure should be avoided. Use mild temperature, short reaction time, and LCMS monitoring. The crude product may initially be isolated as the TFA salt; neutralization or basic workup is required if the neutral amine is desired.

reactants.name: Boc-protected amino heteroaryl oxime ether precursor

reagents.name: Saturated sodium bicarbonate solution, for neutralization/workup

full_recipe.procedure: Dissolve the Boc-protected starting material in dry dichloromethane at approximately 0.05-0.10 M under nitrogen if moisture sensitivity is a concern. Add trifluoroacetic acid slowly at 0-25 °C, preferably starting at 0 °C if the substrate stability is unknown, then allow the mixture to stir at 20-25 °C. Monitor conversion by LCMS or HPLC every 30-60 minutes. Once the Boc starting material is consumed, remove volatile solvent and excess TFA under reduced pressure at low temperature. Co-evaporate with dichloromethane or toluene if needed to remove residual TFA. If the TFA salt is acceptable, purify directly by reverse-phase chromatography or trituration. If the neutral amine is required, dilute the residue with ethyl acetate and carefully neutralize with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate to pH 7-8, keeping gas evolution controlled. Separate layers, extract the aqueous phase with ethyl acetate, combine organic layers, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, concentrate, and purify by chromatography or crystallization. Recommended optimization: use 10 equivalents TFA rather than neat TFA, keep reaction time short, and avoid heating because the oxime ether functionality may be acid-sensitive under harsher conditions.

full_recipe.reaction_name: PBr3-mediated conversion of a benzylic alcohol to a benzylic bromide

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 1st choice / good single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a direct OH-to-Br substitution at a primary benzylic alcohol. PBr3 in dry dichloromethane is chemically plausible and commonly effective for converting benzylic alcohols to benzyl bromides. The ester and aryl sulfonamide should generally tolerate these conditions if the reaction is kept cold during addition and not overexposed to acidic byproducts. Use substoichiometric PBr3 based on its three bromides, dry solvent, inert atmosphere, and careful quench. Avoid large excess PBr3 because the substrate contains an N-sulfonamide and ester and the benzyl bromide product may be acid/labile.
recommendation_and_ranking.note: If decomposition occurs, the best alternative single-step route is Appel bromination using CBr4/PPh3 or NBS/PPh3 in CH2Cl2 at 0-25 °C, but the submitted PBr3 route is reasonable and efficient.

reagents.name: phosphorus tribromide
reagents.quantity_recommendation: 0.40 mmol per 1.00 mmol substrate; approximately 0.043 mL PBr3

procedure: Charge a dry flask under nitrogen with the benzylic alcohol substrate, 1.00 equiv, and dry dichloromethane, 10 mL/mmol.
Cool to 0 °C and add PBr3, 0.40 equiv, dropwise over about 15 minutes.
Stir at 0 °C for 15-30 minutes, then warm to 20-25 °C and stir for about 1-2 hours, monitoring by LCMS or TLC until the alcohol is consumed.
Cool again to 0 °C and carefully quench by slow addition of saturated aqueous NaHCO3 or ice-water, controlling gas evolution and acidity.
Separate the organic layer, extract the aqueous layer with dichloromethane, wash combined organics with brine, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate below 30 °C.
Purify rapidly if needed using neutralized silica or use the benzyl bromide product directly, because benzylic bromides can be moisture- and heat-sensitive.

patent_details: To a mixture of tert-butyl thiazol-4-yl((2,4,5-trifluorophenyl)sulfonyl)carbamate (0.18 g, 0.46 mmol) and (S)-1-benzylpyrrolidin-3-amine (0.08 g, 0.46 mmol) in anhydrous dimethyl sulfoxide (10 mL) was added potassium carbonate (0.19 g, 1.38 mmol) and the reaction mixture was stirred at ambient temperature for 2 h. full_recipe.reaction_name: Regioselective SNAr amination of activated trifluoroaryl sulfonamide

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High; recommended single-step pathway
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is plausible and synthetically appropriate. The aryl fluoride is strongly activated toward SNAr by the sulfonyl-substituted aryl ring and additional fluorine atoms. The chiral aminopyrrolidine nucleophile should selectively displace the most activated para-fluoride to give the observed difluoro-anilino product. K2CO3 in DMF is a reasonable mild basic system to neutralize HF and promote substitution while preserving the Boc/sulfonamide functionality and stereocenter. The recipe is plausible but should be optimized by using dry DMF, slight excess amine, controlled heating, and monitoring to avoid over-substitution or decomposition.

solvents.name: N,N-dimethylformamide
solvents.volume: 8-10 mL per 1 mmol limiting aryl fluoride

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, charge a dry reaction vessel with tert-butyl N-(thiazolyl)-N-[(2,4,5-trifluorophenyl)sulfonyl]carbamate, potassium carbonate, and dry DMF under nitrogen. Add (S)-1-benzyl-3-aminopyrrolidine dropwise or in one portion with stirring. Heat the mixture at 70 °C for approximately 16 h and monitor by LCMS or HPLC until the aryl fluoride starting material is consumed. Cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and filter off inorganic salts. Wash the organic phase with water and brine to remove DMF, dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the SNAr amination product. If conversion is incomplete, extend heating or raise temperature cautiously to 80 °C; avoid large excess amine to minimize potential secondary substitution.

patent_details: To a solution of 4-chloro-3-methoxy-benzaldehyde (25 g, 150 mmol) in toluene (300 mL) was added nitroethane (27 g, 300 mol), dimethylamine hydrochloride (36.5 g, 450 mmol) and potassium fluoride (8.7 g, 150 mmol). The mixture was refluxed for 20 hours with a Dean-Stark trap. The reaction mixture was diluted with ethyl acetate (500 mL) and then quenched with 10% HCl (150 mL). The organic layer was separated, washed with water (150 mL) and brine (150 mL), and then dried over anhydrous Na₂SO₄ and then concentrated under reduced pressure. The residue was purified by column chromatography to give 1-chloro-2-methoxy-4-[2-nitroprop-1-enyl]benzene (20 g) as a yellow solid.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Henry/Knoevenagel-type condensation of substituted benzaldehyde with nitroethane to give a beta-methyl-beta-nitrostyrene

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High plausibility; recommended with optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The target product is an aryl nitroalkene formed by condensation of the chloro-methoxybenzaldehyde with nitroethane. Ammonium acetate is a common mild base/acid buffer catalyst for this transformation. Toluene is acceptable, especially under reflux with water removal. The original recipe is chemically plausible, but nitroethane should be treated as a stoichiometric reactant rather than only a reagent, and ammonium acetate should be used catalytically or substoichiometrically. Removing water improves conversion.

full_recipe.procedure: Charge a dry round-bottom flask with chloro-methoxybenzaldehyde, nitroethane, ammonium acetate, and toluene. Fit with a reflux condenser, preferably using a Dean-Stark trap or other water-removal setup. Heat at reflux around 110 °C for about 6 h while monitoring by TLC, HPLC, or LC-MS. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, wash with water and brine, dry the organic layer over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude beta-methyl-beta-nitrostyrene product by silica gel chromatography or recrystallization if suitable. Expected product is mainly the thermodynamically favored E-nitroalkene.

full_recipe.reaction_name: TBAF-mediated tert-butyldimethylsilyl ether deprotection to primary alcohol

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 1 / 1: recommended and plausible single-step pathway
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The transformation is a standard fluoride-promoted cleavage of a TBS-protected primary alcohol to the free alcohol. Tetrabutylammonium fluoride in THF is well matched to this substrate and should be chemoselective; the amide, morpholine, heteroaryl, and cyclic ether motifs are expected to tolerate mild room-temperature fluoride conditions. Avoid excess time, heat, or highly wet/basic conditions to minimize side reactions.

reagents.name: Tetrabutylammonium fluoride, preferably 1.0 M in THF

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the TBS-protected substrate in dry THF at about 0.1 M concentration. Add tetrabutylammonium fluoride solution in THF slowly at 20 °C, using about 1.5 equivalents. Stir at 20 °C for 1–2 hours and monitor by LCMS or TLC until complete consumption of starting material. Quench with saturated aqueous NH4Cl or water, dilute with ethyl acetate, separate the layers, and wash the organic phase with brine. Dry over Na2SO4, filter, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the free primary alcohol product: CC1(CO)Cc2cc(NC(=O)c3cnn4cccnc34)c(N3CCOCC3)nc2O1. full_recipe.reaction_name: Acid-promoted cyclocondensation of N-phenacyl anthranilamide with ammonium thiocyanate to a quinazolinethione

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / Rank 1 for this single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed pathway is chemically plausible: ammonium thiocyanate under acetic acid generates thiocyanic/isothiocyanic acid equivalents, allowing the ortho-amino benzamide substrate to form a thiourea-type intermediate followed by intramolecular cyclodehydration to the quinazolinethione product. full_recipe.procedure: Charge a dry round-bottom flask with 2-amino-N-[2-(4-bromophenyl)-2-oxoethyl]benzamide, ammonium thiocyanate, and ethanol. Add glacial acetic acid, fit the flask with a condenser, and heat at ethanol reflux, approximately 78 °C, for about 8 hours. Monitor conversion by TLC or LC-MS. After completion, cool to room temperature, then pour the mixture into cold water. If needed, adjust to near neutral pH with aqueous sodium bicarbonate. Collect the precipitated solid by filtration, wash with water and cold ethanol, and dry. Purify by recrystallization from ethanol/DMF or by silica chromatography if necessary.

full_recipe.reaction_name: SNAr benzylamination of an activated chloro-nitro heteroarene

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / recommended with optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The pathway is chemically plausible: the chloro heteroarene is activated toward nucleophilic aromatic substitution by the ring nitrogen and nitro substituent, and benzylamine is an appropriate nucleophile. full_recipe.reaction_name: Hydrazone formation / Schiff-base condensation of substituted furfural aldehyde with heteroaryl hydrazine

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended optimized route: 1st choice; submitted piperidine/EtOH route: 2nd choice
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The transformation is chemically plausible: the aldehyde CCc1ccc(C=O)o1 condenses with the hydrazine derivative NNc1ncnc2c1cnn2-c1ccccc1 to give the corresponding C=N–NH heteroaryl hydrazone. However, piperidine in ethanol is not ideal for this specific condensation; mild acid catalysis is generally better for hydrazone formation because it activates the aldehyde and promotes dehydration. Strong acid should be avoided because the heteroaryl hydrazine can be protonated/deactivated. Recommended single-step retrosynthesis is exactly the submitted disconnection: target hydrazone from the aldehyde plus the heteroaryl hydrazine, using EtOH with catalytic AcOH under reflux. Molecular sieves or azeotropic/removal of water can improve conversion.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol aldehyde scale, charge a dry round-bottom flask with CCc1ccc(C=O)o1 aldehyde, 1.0 equiv, and heteroaryl hydrazine NNc1ncnc2c1cnn2-c1ccccc1, 1.05 equiv. Add ethanol, 10 mL per mmol aldehyde, followed by acetic acid, 0.2 equiv. Optionally add activated 4 Å molecular sieves to help remove water. Stir and heat at ethanol reflux, about 78 °C, for 4 h. Monitor by TLC or LCMS for disappearance of aldehyde. After completion, cool to room temperature. If product precipitates, collect by filtration, wash with cold ethanol, and dry under vacuum. If no precipitate forms, concentrate the mixture and purify by trituration or flash chromatography using a suitable ethyl acetate/hexane or dichloromethane/methanol system. The expected product is CCc1ccc(C=NNc2ncnc3c2cnn3-c2ccccc2)o1, potentially as an E/Z hydrazone mixture with the E-isomer often favored.

patent_details: 2-chloro-9-[[4-[1-ethyl-4-(trifluoromethyl)imidazol-2-yl]phenyl]methyl]-7-methyl-purin-8-imine (0.40 g, 918 μmol), (2-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)boronic acid (349 mg, 1.84 mmol) and cesium carbonate (1.20 g, 3.67 mmol) were mixed in water (4 mL) and dioxane (20 mL). full_recipe.reaction_name: HATU/DIPEA-mediated amide coupling of heteroaryl carboxylic acid with chiral bicyclic amine hydrochloride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High priority / Rank 1
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a direct carboxylic acid-to-amide coupling. The starting acid and the chiral amine hydrochloride match the product connectivity exactly. HATU with DIPEA in DMF is a plausible and commonly effective system for coupling heteroaryl carboxylic acids with sterically constrained amines. DIPEA is needed both to liberate the free amine from its HCl salt and to promote coupling. This recipe is chemically sound and likely optimal as a first attempt. Main risks are incomplete conversion due to steric hindrance of the bicyclic amine and possible solubility issues, but these can usually be addressed by using slight excess amine/HATU and sufficient base.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the heteroaryl carboxylic acid substrate in dry DMF to approximately 0.1 M concentration. Add DIPEA, followed by HATU, and stir for 10-15 minutes at room temperature to activate the acid. Add the chiral bicyclic amine hydrochloride in one portion or as a DMF solution. Stir at 25 °C for about 12 hours and monitor conversion by LC-MS or HPLC. After completion, dilute with ethyl acetate and wash sequentially with water, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine. Dry the organic layer over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the target amide product: [2H]C([2H])([2H])N(Cc1ccc(OC)cc1)c1cc(Cl)nn2c(C(=O)N[C@@H]3C[C@H]4CCO[C@H]43)cnc12.

recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The transformation is chemically plausible: the aryl amine precursor can be converted to the aryl iodide through diazotization followed by iodide substitution. However, the provided recipe uses nitrite and iodide only in water and lacks acid, which is essential for forming the diazonium intermediate. Water alone may also give poor solubility for this polycyclic lactam substrate. procedure: Charge the aryl amine precursor, water, and acetonitrile to a reaction flask and cool to 0-5 °C.

Add potassium iodide portionwise or as a concentrated aqueous solution at 0-5 °C. Gas evolution and darkening may occur.
Allow the mixture to warm to 20-25 °C and stir for 1.5-3 hours until the amine is consumed.
Quench residual iodine with aqueous sodium thiosulfate if needed, then extract with ethyl acetate or dichloromethane.

Wash the organic layer with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or crystallization to obtain the aryl iodide product: O=C1Nc2ncccc2[C@]12Cc1ccc(I)cc1C2.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Mitsunobu O-alkylation of substituted phenol with benzylic alcohol

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High priority / Rank 1 for this single-step ether formation
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed pathway is chemically plausible and well matched to the target transformation: a substituted phenol reacts with a primary benzylic alcohol under Mitsunobu conditions using tributylphosphine and ADDP in THF to form the aryl benzyl ether. The phenol is sufficiently acidic for Mitsunobu activation, and the alcohol is primary/benzylic, so ether formation should be favored. The ethyl ester and fluoroaryl benzofuran motifs are compatible with these mild, neutral conditions. Possible issues include steric hindrance around the phenol and formation of phosphine oxide/ADDP hydrazide byproducts, but overall this is a good route.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, charge a dry reaction flask with ethyl 3-(4-hydroxy-3,5-dimethylphenyl)propanoate, the benzylic alcohol, and dry THF. Cool to 0 °C if convenient, then add tributylphosphine followed by ADDP portionwise. Allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C and stir for about 16 h. Monitor by LCMS or TLC for disappearance of the phenol/alcohol. After completion, concentrate the mixture and purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography, for example using hexanes/ethyl acetate gradient, to afford the desired aryl benzyl ether: CCOC(=O)CCc1ccc(OCc2cc(F)cc3c(F)c(C)oc23)c(C)c1C. This recipe is recommended as written; if optimization is needed, use 1.3 equivalents each of tributylphosphine and ADDP or switch to PPh3/DIAD as a secondary Mitsunobu option, though the given PBu3/ADDP system is generally strong and suitable.

patent_details: Sodium hydride (15.2 mg, 0.38 mmol) was added in portions to a stirred solution of (R)-7-((2-chloro-6-fluorobenzyl)oxy)-1-((3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)sulfonyl)-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinolin-3-ol (100 mg, 0.19 mmol) in N,N-dimethylformamide (10 mL) at 0°C. Methyl 2-bromo-2-methylpropanoate (69 mg, 0.38 mmol) was added dropwise and the resulting solution was stirred for thirty minutes at 0°C. The mixture was warmed to room temperature and stirred an additional two hours. Water was added, and the mixture was extracted three times with ethyl acetate. The combined organic layers were washed three times with water, brine, dried ( Na₂SO₄), and concentrated. The resulting residue was purified via MPLC eluting with a gradient of 5-50% ethyl acetate in petroleum ether to afford methyl (R)-2-((7-((2-chloro-6-fluorobenzyl)oxy)-1-((3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)sulfonyl)-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinolin-3-yl)oxy)-2-methylpropanoate (35 mg, 29%) as a yellow oil.

full_recipe.reaction_name: N-sulfonylation of a secondary tetrahydroquinoline amine with 3-(trifluoromethyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Rank 1: Plausible and recommended single-step pathway
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The starting material contains a secondary cyclic aniline/tetrahydroquinoline N-H, which should react directly with the arylsulfonyl chloride to give the N-sulfonamide product. Pyridine is suitable as both solvent and HCl scavenger. The apparent stereochemical change from [C@H] to [C@@H] is likely due to different SMILES atom ordering rather than true inversion, since the stereocenter is not involved in the reaction. Recommended optimization: use dry pyridine, slight excess sulfonyl chloride, start at 0 °C then warm to room temperature under inert atmosphere.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve the secondary amine substrate in anhydrous pyridine at approximately 0.2 M concentration, using about 5 mL pyridine per 1 mmol substrate. Cool the solution to 0 °C. Add 1.2 equivalents of 3-(trifluoromethyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride portionwise or dropwise while maintaining 0 °C. After addition, allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C and stir for 4 to 16 hours, monitoring by LC-MS or TLC. Upon completion, quench by slow addition into cold aqueous ammonium chloride or dilute aqueous acid, then extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the organic phase with dilute HCl to remove pyridine, then saturated sodium bicarbonate and brine. Dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography to afford the N-sulfonylated product.

patent_details: 1-Hydroxybenzotriazole (273 mg, 2.0 mmol), benzylamine (0.109 ml, 1.0 mmol) and N-methylmorpholine (0.222 ml, 2.0 mmol) were added to a solution of (4-dimethylamino-4-phenylcyclohexylidene)acetic acid hydrochloride (296 mg, 1.0 mmol) in dry dimethylformamide (10 ml) under argon. The solution was cooled to 0°C. and dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (417 mg, 2.0 mmol) was added. The reaction mixture was stirred at RT for 12 d. Working up of the mixture was carried out by separating off the urea which had precipitated out and introducing the filtrate into a mixture of saturated NaCl solution (40 ml) and saturated NaHCO₃ solution (10 ml). Still further urea thereby precipitated out and was separated off. 5 M sodium hydroxide solution (4 ml, 20 mmol) was added to the aqueous phase and the mixture was diluted with water (300 ml) and stored at 5°C. for 3 d. The product thereby precipitated out as a colourless solid in a yield of 65% (227 mg) and with an m.p. of 145-148°C.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Wittig olefination of a hindered cyclohexanone with N-benzyl-2-(triphenylphosphoranylidene)acetamide

recommendation_and_ranking.overall_assessment: The proposed C=O to C=C conversion is chemically plausible: the stabilized amide ylide should olefinate the cyclohexanone to give the exocyclic alpha,beta-unsaturated amide. However, NaH is not optimal when the ylide is already supplied; it can deprotonate the amide N-H and create solubility/side-reaction issues. Use the preformed ylide under dry, heated, neutral Wittig conditions.

ranking.recipe: Optimized: ketone + preformed stabilized Wittig ylide in anhydrous THF, reflux, no NaH
ranking.rationale: Most direct single-step route from the stated reactants. Avoids unnecessary strong base and should favor the E-alkene typical of stabilized ylides.

ranking.recipe: Submitted: ketone + ylide + NaH in THF
ranking.rationale: Plausible but less clean; NaH is unnecessary for a preformed ylide and may deprotonate the secondary amide or complicate conversion/workup.

procedure: Under dry nitrogen or argon, charge a dry flask with N,N-dimethyl-1-phenyl-4-oxocyclohexan-1-amine, 1.0 equiv.
Add N-benzyl-2-(triphenylphosphoranylidene)acetamide, 1.2 equiv, followed by anhydrous THF at about 0.10 M concentration, e.g. 10 mL THF per 1 mmol ketone.
Heat at THF reflux, about 66 °C, for 18 h while monitoring by TLC, LC-MS, or HPLC.
If ketone remains, add an additional 0.2 equiv of ylide and continue reflux for 4-8 h.

Cool to room temperature, remove THF under reduced pressure, and purify the crude material by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC, separating triphenylphosphine oxide from the desired alkene product.
Recommended change from the submitted recipe: omit NaH unless starting from the corresponding phosphonium salt rather than the isolated ylide.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Thionyl chloride conversion of secondary heteroaryl alcohol to alkyl chloride

ranking.pathway: Optimized SOCl2 chlorination using base in dry toluene
ranking.rationale: The target transformation is a direct alcohol-to-chloride substitution. SOCl2 is appropriate, and dry toluene is acceptable for this lipophilic substrate. Adding pyridine or 2,6-lutidine is recommended to trap HCl/SO2-derived acid, reduce elimination or benzylic cation side reactions, and improve cleanliness.

ranking.pathway: Original recipe: SOCl2 in toluene without base
ranking.rationale: Chemically plausible, but less optimal. The substrate is a secondary heteroaryl/benzylic-type alcohol, so strongly acidic conditions from generated HCl may cause elimination, partial decomposition, or side reactions. It may still work if run cold and monitored carefully.

ranking.pathway: Alternative Appel-type chlorination, e.g. PPh3/CCl4 or PPh3/NCS
ranking.rationale: Could convert the alcohol to chloride under milder neutral conditions, but generates more waste and may complicate purification for this hydrophobic substrate.

recommendation_and_ranking.overall_recommendation: Use the same single-step retrosynthetic disconnection from the chloride back to the corresponding secondary alcohol, but optimize the forward recipe by adding a hindered/non-nucleophilic base and using dry solvent under inert atmosphere. Avoid high temperature unless conversion is poor.

reactants.name: CCc1sc(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)cc1C(O)C1CCCCC1
reactants.volume: not applicable; weigh according to molecular weight

procedure: Dry the reaction flask and maintain an inert nitrogen or argon atmosphere.
Dissolve the alcohol substrate, CCc1sc(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)cc1C(O)C1CCCCC1, in dry toluene at about 10 mL per 1 mmol substrate.
Cool the solution to 0 °C.
Add pyridine, 1.5 equivalents, slowly with stirring.
Add thionyl chloride, 1.2 equivalents, dropwise at 0 °C. Gas evolution of SO2/HCl may occur; use a well-ventilated fume hood.
After addition, allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 2 hours.
Monitor conversion by TLC, LCMS, or HPLC. If starting alcohol remains, stir up to 6 hours at 25 °C or add a small additional portion of SOCl2, about 0.2 equivalents.
When complete, cautiously quench by slow addition into ice-cold saturated aqueous NaHCO3, maintaining good ventilation and controlling gas evolution.
Separate the organic layer, wash with water and brine, dry over Na2SO4 or MgSO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or trituration as appropriate to obtain CCc1sc(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)cc1C(Cl)C1CCCCC1.

Note: If stereochemistry at the alcohol carbon is important, this SOCl2 method may give inversion, retention, or partial racemization depending on conditions; verify stereochemical outcome experimentally.

full_recipe.reaction_name: HATU/DIPEA-mediated amide coupling of primary amine substrate with 3-bromobenzoic acid

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Rank 1 / Recommended
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a direct amide bond formation between a primary aliphatic amine and 3-bromobenzoic acid. The provided conditions, HATU with DIPEA in DMF, are highly plausible and commonly effective for this type of coupling. The aryl bromide is compatible, and the aliphatic amine should be more nucleophilic than the anilino/heteroaryl NH, giving good chemoselectivity. Minor risk exists for competing acylation of the anilino NH or incomplete conversion due to steric/electronic effects, but overall this is a strong single-step retrosynthetic route.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve the amine substrate in dry DMF. Add 3-bromobenzoic acid, followed by DIPEA. Cool to 0 °C if necessary during addition, then add HATU portionwise. Allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for approximately 12 hours. Monitor by LCMS or HPLC until the amine is consumed. Quench with water, extract with ethyl acetate or purify directly by reverse-phase chromatography/preparative HPLC if polar. Wash organic layers with water and brine, dry, concentrate, and purify to afford the target amide product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Selective N-mesylation of aromatic amine with methanesulfonyl chloride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good but not ideal as originally specified; recommended optimized single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is chemically plausible: the primary aromatic amine should react with methanesulfonyl chloride to give the aryl methanesulfonamide. However, using pyridine as the only solvent can increase exposure to basic sulfonylating conditions and may cause competing indole N-mesylation or over-mesylation. A more controlled protocol is to use dry dichloromethane as solvent, pyridine as base, slow addition of near-stoichiometric methanesulfonyl chloride at 0 °C, then warm to room temperature.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the amino-indole substrate in dry dichloromethane at about 0.05–0.07 M concentration. Cool the solution to 0 °C. Add pyridine, then add methanesulfonyl chloride dropwise while maintaining 0 °C. Stir at 0 °C for 30 minutes, then allow the reaction to warm to 20 °C and stir for about 2–3 hours. Monitor by LCMS or TLC for consumption of the amine and avoid prolonged reaction time to minimize indole N-mesylation or bis-sulfonylation. Quench with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride or water at 0–20 °C. Separate the organic phase, wash with dilute acid to remove pyridine, then with sodium bicarbonate and brine. Dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or crystallization to obtain the desired methanesulfonamide product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: MOM ether protection of a primary alcohol using chloromethyl methyl ether

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended with optimization; original recipe ranked 2/3, optimized recipe ranked 1/3
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The transformation is a plausible single-step protection of the terminal primary alcohol as a methoxymethyl ether. The lipid ether/alkene framework should tolerate mildly basic MOM protection conditions. The original DIPEA/MOMCl/DCM recipe is chemically reasonable but not optimal because neutral alcohols can react slowly with MOMCl/DIPEA alone, and strict dryness is needed. Adding catalytic iodide such as TBAI improves conversion by forming a more reactive MOM iodide equivalent in situ. Use anhydrous dichloromethane at 0 °C to room temperature with excess DIPEA to suppress acid-mediated alkene or MOM cleavage issues. Major concern: chloromethyl methyl ether is highly toxic/carcinogenic and must be handled only in a well-controlled fume hood.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve the lipid primary alcohol precursor in anhydrous dichloromethane at about 0.1 M concentration. Cool to 0 °C. Add DIPEA, then catalytic TBAI, and slowly add chloromethyl methyl ether while maintaining 0 °C. Stir for 15 min at 0 °C, then allow the reaction to warm to room temperature and stir for about 12 h, monitoring by TLC, LC-MS, or NMR for disappearance of the alcohol. Quench carefully at 0 °C with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate or ammonium chloride, separate the organic phase, wash with brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify by flash chromatography on neutralized silica gel using hexane/ethyl acetate mixtures to give the MOM-protected product: CCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCCCCCOC[C@H](CCOCOC)OCCCCCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCC.

full_recipe.reaction_name: SNAr amination of chlorinated aminopyrimidine with N-methyl-2-fluoroethylamine

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / Rank 1 among simple single-step options
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed pathway is chemically plausible: the chloro-aminopyrimidine is activated toward nucleophilic aromatic substitution by ring nitrogens, and CNCCF is a suitable secondary amine nucleophile to give CN(CCF)c1ccnc(N)n1. Triethylamine can neutralize HCl, and ethanol is acceptable. The recipe is not maximally optimized because ethanol may slow SNAr and the amine is volatile/reactive; mild heating at ethanol reflux with slight excess amine and base is recommended. If conversion is poor, switch to i-PrOH, MeCN, or DMF and heat to 80-100 °C.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry flask with Nc1nccc(Cl)n1, ethanol, N-methyl-2-fluoroethylamine, and triethylamine. Heat at ethanol reflux, approximately 78 °C, for 12 h with stirring. Monitor by LCMS or HPLC for disappearance of the chloropyrimidine. After completion, cool to room temperature, remove ethanol under reduced pressure, dilute with ethyl acetate or dichloromethane, and wash with water/brine. Dry the organic phase, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford CN(CCF)c1ccnc(N)n1. If conversion is incomplete, extend to 18-24 h or run in sealed vessel in i-PrOH/MeCN at 85-100 °C.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Regioselective SNAr amination of activated dichloropyridine sulfonamide

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High priority / Rank 1: plausible and recommended with mild optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The pathway is chemically plausible: the dichloropyridine sulfonamide is strongly activated toward nucleophilic aromatic substitution by the pyridine nitrogen and sulfonyl substituent. The chiral piperidinyl amine should selectively displace the more activated chloro position to give the mono-aminated chloropyridine product. K2CO3 in DMF is a reasonable base/solvent system. Recommended optimization is to use slight excess amine, 2–3 equiv K2CO3, dry DMF, and heat at 75–90 °C while monitoring for over-substitution or decomposition.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry reaction flask with the dichloropyridine sulfonamide electrophile, the chiral piperidinyl amine nucleophile, and potassium carbonate. Add dry DMF to give approximately 0.2 M concentration. Stir the mixture at 80 °C for 6–16 hours and monitor by LCMS or HPLC until the electrophile is consumed. Cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and filter off inorganic salts. Wash the organic phase with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the mono-aminated chloropyridine product. Avoid excessive heating or large excess amine to minimize possible bis-amination or decomposition.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Grignard methylation of a cyclopentadienyl titanium trichloride complex to the corresponding trimethyl titanium complex

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good but moisture/temperature sensitive; ranked 4/5 for plausibility
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The proposed transformation is chemically plausible: three Ti-Cl bonds in the titanium trichloride precursor can be replaced by methyl groups using approximately 3 equivalents of methylmagnesium bromide. THF is an appropriate coordinating solvent for Grignard-mediated transmetallation. However, the product TiMe3 complex is likely highly air-, moisture-, and thermally sensitive, and excess Grignard reagent or warming too quickly may cause decomposition or ligand attack. The recipe should be optimized by using strictly anhydrous/inert conditions, low-temperature addition, and only slight excess MeMgBr.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, dry all glassware thoroughly and maintain a nitrogen or argon atmosphere throughout. Charge a Schlenk flask with the titanium trichloride complex, using 1.0 equivalent, and dissolve or suspend it in 20 mL of anhydrous THF. Cool the mixture to -78 °C. Add methylmagnesium bromide in THF slowly, using 3.05 equivalents, while maintaining the temperature below -60 °C. After addition, stir at -78 °C for 1 hour, then allow the mixture to warm gradually to 0 °C and stir for an additional 2 hours. Monitor conversion if possible by low-temperature NMR or by disappearance of the starting titanium chloride complex. Remove insoluble magnesium salts by cannula filtration under inert atmosphere through a dry frit or Celite pad. Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure at low temperature and handle the crude trimethyl titanium product strictly under inert atmosphere. Avoid aqueous quench, air exposure, and prolonged warming because the product is expected to be highly sensitive.

full_recipe.reaction_name: N-methoxycarbonylation of 4-pentadecylaniline with methyl chloroformate

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High plausibility; recommended with optimization. Original pyridine-solvent recipe: 3.5/5. Optimized DCM/Et3N/DMAP recipe: 4.5/5.
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is a straightforward carbamate formation from an aniline and methyl chloroformate. The proposed reagent, methyl chloroformate, is appropriate, and pyridine can act as both solvent and base to trap HCl. However, pyridine as bulk solvent is not optimal due to difficult removal, odor, and possible slower reaction/workup issues. A better single-step protocol is to use dry dichloromethane as solvent, triethylamine or DIPEA as base, and catalytic DMAP, adding methyl chloroformate at 0 °C then warming to room temperature. This should give the methyl aryl carbamate cleanly.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve 1.0 equiv of 4-pentadecylaniline in dry dichloromethane, using about 10 mL solvent per mmol of amine. Add 1.5 equiv triethylamine and 0.05 equiv DMAP. Cool the mixture to 0 °C. Add 1.1 equiv methyl chloroformate dropwise while maintaining 0–5 °C. After addition, allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C and stir for about 3 hours, monitoring by TLC or LCMS until the aniline is consumed. Quench carefully with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride or water, separate the organic layer, wash with dilute HCl to remove amine base, then saturated sodium bicarbonate and brine.
