recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended; ranked 1/1 for this single-step transformation
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed pathway is plausible and suitable. N-bromosuccinimide in DMF is a standard mild system for electrophilic bromination of electron-rich heteroarenes such as furans. The substrate contains a 2-substituted furan, and bromination is expected at the remaining electron-rich 5-position to give the target bromofuran. Main risks are over-bromination, bromination/addition at the activated alkene, or E/Z isomerization, so low temperature, near-stoichiometric NBS, and short reaction time are recommended.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.00 mmol scale, dissolve methyl 2-acetamido-3-(furan-2-yl)acrylate in dry DMF, using about 10 mL DMF per mmol of substrate. Stir for 30 minutes at 0 °C, then allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C and stir for about 1.5 additional hours. Monitor by TLC or LC-MS until starting material is consumed. Quench with aqueous sodium thiosulfate, dilute with water, and extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the organic layer with water and brine to remove DMF, dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography to obtain methyl 2-acetamido-3-(5-bromofuran-2-yl)acrylate.

recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed reactant is a chiral Schöllkopf-type bis-lactim ether. n-BuLi in THF can deprotonate the acidic alpha-position, but the original recipe is not plausible as written because no electrophile is present to install the 4,4,4-trifluoro-3-phenylbutyl substituent. The optimized route is deprotonation with n-BuLi at low temperature followed by SN2 alkylation with 1-bromo-4,4,4-trifluoro-3-phenylbutane or the corresponding iodide/tosylate. Cool to -78 °C. Add n-BuLi, 1.10 equiv, dropwise while maintaining -78 °C, then stir for 30-60 min to form the lithium enolate. Add DMPU, 1.0 equiv, if needed, followed by dropwise addition of 1-bromo-4,4,4-trifluoro-3-phenylbutane, 1.3 equiv, in a small amount of THF. Stir at -78 °C for 1 h, then allow the mixture to warm gradually to -40 to 0 °C over 3 h. full_recipe.reaction_name: Selective N-triflylation of an aryl amine with triflic anhydride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Optimized recipe: 4/5; submitted recipe without base: 2/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is chemically plausible: the primary aryl amine can be converted to the corresponding N-triflyl sulfonamide using triflic anhydride. However, the submitted conditions list only triflic anhydride in dichloromethane and omit a base. Without base, triflic acid formation can protonate the aniline, reduce conversion, and damage the acid-sensitive 1,4-dihydropyridine core. A dry, low-temperature reaction with a hindered non-nucleophilic base such as 2,6-lutidine is recommended. Use slight excess triflic anhydride to minimize over-reaction and competing sulfonylation.

procedure: Dry the reaction vessel and maintain under nitrogen or argon.
Dissolve the aniline-containing dihydropyridine substrate, 1.00 equiv, in anhydrous dichloromethane at approximately 0.1 M concentration.
Cool the solution to -20 °C.
Add 2,6-lutidine, 2.5 equiv, slowly while maintaining the temperature below -20 °C.
Add triflic anhydride, 1.05 equiv, dropwise at -20 °C.
Stir at -20 °C for 30–60 minutes, then allow the reaction to warm to 0 °C and stir for an additional 2–3 hours.
Monitor by LC-MS or HPLC for disappearance of the starting aniline and formation of the N-triflyl product.
Quench carefully at 0 °C with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate solution.
Separate the organic phase, wash with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
Purify by silica gel chromatography using a mild gradient such as dichloromethane/methanol with 0.1% triethylamine if needed to reduce decomposition or tailing.

procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, charge a dry flask with C#CCNC1=NC(=O)SC1, the aldehyde O=CC1CC2CC(C1)CN(Cc1ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc1C(F)(F)F)C2, and isopropanol at 10 mL/mmol.
Add piperidine 0.2 equiv and acetic acid 0.2 equiv. Alternatively, use preformed piperidinium acetate, C1CC[NH2+]CC1.CC(=O)[O-], 0.2 equiv.
Heat at reflux, approximately 82 °C, for 6–12 h under nitrogen or air, monitoring by LCMS or HPLC.
If conversion stalls, extend to 16 h or add activated 4 Å molecular sieves to reduce water and drive the condensation.
Cool to room temperature. Concentrate or precipitate by addition of water/antisolvent if suitable.
Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to isolate C#CCNC1=NC(=O)S/C1=C\C1CC2CC(C1)CN(Cc1ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc1C(F)(F)F)C2, checking E/Z purity.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of an aryl pinacol boronate with a hindered aryl bromide

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Original recipe: low plausibility, 1/5; optimized single-step route: recommended, 4/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The retrosynthesis is correct: the product is formed by coupling the aryl-Bpin fragment with the aryl bromide fragment. However, the given forward recipe contains only K2CO3 in toluene/water and lacks a palladium catalyst/ligand, so the coupling is not expected to proceed efficiently. Because both coupling partners are sterically hindered and electron-rich, a more active Pd/XPhos-type Suzuki system is recommended. The chiral ether/ester framework should be compatible with mild aqueous base and neutral Suzuki conditions.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, charge a dry sealed tube with the aryl pinacol boronate substrate, the aryl bromide coupling partner, potassium phosphate tribasic, Pd(OAc)2, and XPhos. Add degassed toluene and degassed water, seal, and heat at 90 °C for 16 h with vigorous stirring. Monitor conversion by LC-MS or HPLC. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, filter through Celite to remove inorganic salts and palladium residues, and wash the organic phase with water and brine. Dry over Na2SO4, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to obtain the biaryl product. If conversion is incomplete, extend to 24 h or increase catalyst loading to 7.5 mol% Pd(OAc)2/15 mol% XPhos.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Reductive amination of pyridyl aldehyde with primary amine to give secondary benzylamine

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended optimized route: 1st choice; original NaBH4/MeOH recipe: 2nd choice
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The disconnection is correct: the product is best made in one step by reductive amination of CCc1cc(C=O)ccn1 with NCCN1Cc2ccc(F)cc2CC1Cc1ccc(F)cc1. However, NaBH4 in methanol is only moderately suitable because it can directly reduce the aldehyde to the alcohol before imine/iminium formation. A more selective and standard single-step recipe is NaBH(OAc)3-mediated reductive amination under mildly acidic conditions in DCE/MeOH. This should improve chemoselectivity and conversion for this hindered, basic amine substrate.

full_recipe.reaction_name: DMAP/acetic anhydride promoted aldehyde-mediated dearomatizing cyclization/acetoxylation to an aryltetralin-type acetate

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Corrected single-step route: moderate plausibility; original recipe as written: not plausible
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The submitted recipe is incomplete because the product contains a 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl group that is absent from the listed reactant/reagents. Acetic anhydride and DMAP can account for acetylation, but not for installation of the aryl group. The missing required carbon/aryl source is most plausibly 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzaldehyde. With this aldehyde included, the pathway becomes a plausible one-pot electrophilic dearomatizing cyclization/acetoxylation of the electron-rich benzodioxane arene, although selectivity and yield may be substrate-sensitive.

full_recipe.procedure: Under dry nitrogen, charge a dry flask with N-methyl-3-(2,3-dihydrobenzo[b][1,4]dioxin-6-yl)propanamide, 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzaldehyde, and anhydrous toluene. Add DMAP, then acetic anhydride slowly at room temperature. Heat at toluene reflux, about 110 °C, for 18 h and monitor by TLC or LCMS. After completion, cool to room temperature and carefully quench with saturated aqueous NaHCO3. Extract with ethyl acetate, wash the organic layer with water and brine, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography, for example hexane/ethyl acetate gradient, to isolate the target acetoxy aryltetralin-type product. The original recipe without 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzaldehyde should not be used because it cannot form the stated product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Thionyl chloride conversion of heteroarylmethanol to chloromethyl heteroarene

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 1/3, recommended single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed alcohol-to-alkyl chloride transformation using SOCl2 is chemically plausible and likely effective for converting the hydroxymethyl oxazole precursor to the chloromethyl product. Use dry CH2Cl2, low-temperature addition, and mild conditions to reduce HCl-promoted decomposition or sulfonamide/heteroarene side reactions. Catalytic DMF is recommended to activate SOCl2 and improve conversion. Alternative Appel or mesylate/chloride routes are possible but less atom-economical or require extra steps.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the hydroxymethyl starting material, 1.0 equiv, in anhydrous dichloromethane, about 10 mL per mmol. Cool to 0 °C. Add catalytic DMF, 0.05 equiv, then add thionyl chloride, 1.5 equiv, dropwise while maintaining 0 °C. Stir at 0 °C for 30 min, then warm to 20–25 °C and stir for about 2–3 h, monitoring by LCMS or TLC. After completion, remove volatile SOCl2 and solvent under reduced pressure below 30 °C. Co-evaporate with dry toluene if needed. Dissolve the residue in ethyl acetate, wash rapidly with cold saturated NaHCO3 and brine, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate. Purify quickly by flash chromatography using a small amount of base-modified eluent if needed to afford NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(-c2oc(CCl)nc2-c2ccccc2)cc1.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Amide bond formation via oxalyl-chloride acid-chloride activation

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Supplied recipe: 3/5; optimized recipe: 4/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The retrosynthesis is logical: the target amide can be made from 1-methylpyrrole-carboxylic acid and the corresponding aniline by acid activation. Oxalyl chloride is a plausible reagent to form the acid chloride, followed by coupling with the aniline. However, the supplied recipe is not optimal because no base is specified to neutralize HCl, and DMA can react with oxalyl chloride if present during acid-chloride formation. Recommended optimization is staged addition: form the acid chloride in dry THF with oxalyl chloride and catalytic DMF, remove excess oxalyl chloride, then add the aniline with DIPEA in THF/DMA.

procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, suspend or dissolve 1.05 equiv of 1-methyl-1H-pyrrole-2-carboxylic acid in dry THF at 0 °C.
Add catalytic DMF, then slowly add 1.3 equiv oxalyl chloride while maintaining 0 °C. Allow the mixture to warm to 20–25 °C and stir for about 2 h until acid-chloride formation is complete.
Remove excess oxalyl chloride and volatile byproducts under reduced pressure, preferably co-evaporating with dry THF to give the crude acid chloride.
In a separate flask, dissolve 1.0 equiv of the aniline coupling partner in dry THF/DMA and cool to 0 °C.
Add 2.5 equiv DIPEA, then slowly add the acid chloride solution or suspension.
Warm to 25 °C and stir for 12 h. Monitor by LCMS or HPLC.

Quench carefully with water or saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate, extract with ethyl acetate or suitable organic solvent, wash, dry, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the target amide.
Avoid adding DMA during the oxalyl-chloride activation stage because it may react with oxalyl chloride and reduce reproducibility.

full_recipe.reaction_name: BCl3-mediated debenzylation of aryl benzyl ethers to diphenol

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Rank 2/5: plausible but not the most chemoselectively optimal
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is global cleavage of two aryl benzyl ethers to the corresponding phenols. BCl3 in dichloromethane is a credible single-step method for benzyl aryl ether cleavage. However, the substrate also contains an anisole methoxy group, an isoxazole, and an aryl chloride; BCl3 can be harsh and may partially demethylate the anisole or cause Lewis-acid-promoted decomposition if warmed or over-treated. The pathway is plausible if run cold with controlled equivalents and short reaction time. A potentially milder alternative is catalytic hydrogenolysis, but that carries risk of aryl chloride reduction and heteroaryl/isoxazole sensitivity. Therefore, optimized BCl3 conditions are acceptable, but require careful low-temperature control.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve the bis(benzyl ether) precursor in anhydrous dichloromethane at approximately 0.1 M concentration. Cool the solution to -78 °C. Add 1.0 M BCl3 in dichloromethane dropwise, using 3.0 equivalents total. Stir at -78 °C for about 2 hours, then allow the mixture to warm slowly to 0 °C over about 1 hour while monitoring by LCMS or TLC. If starting material remains, an additional 0.5-1.0 equivalent of BCl3 may be added at -78 °C. After completion, carefully quench at -78 to 0 °C by slow addition of methanol, followed by saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate. Extract with ethyl acetate or dichloromethane, wash with brine, dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford COc1ccc(-c2c(C)noc2-c2cc(Cl)c(O)cc2O)cc1. Avoid warming strongly or using large excess BCl3 to minimize anisole demethylation.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Williamson ether synthesis: O-alkylation of vanillin with 11-bromoundecan-1-ol

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / recommended with minor optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed pathway is chemically plausible: vanillin phenol is deprotonated by K2CO3 and undergoes SN2 alkylation with the primary bromide of 11-bromoundecan-1-ol to give the aryl alkyl ether while retaining the terminal alcohol. Acetone is acceptable for Williamson ether formation, and the aldehyde should tolerate these mild basic conditions. Main limitations are moderate reaction rate due to heterogeneous K2CO3 and possible low solubility of the long-chain bromoalcohol. Adding catalytic KI or TBAI and using dry acetone or acetonitrile improves conversion. Strong bases are not recommended because of aldehyde sensitivity.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, charge a dry round-bottom flask with vanillin, 11-bromoundecan-1-ol, anhydrous K2CO3, catalytic KI, and dry acetone. Stir the suspension under nitrogen or a dry atmosphere and heat at reflux, approximately 56 °C, for 12–18 h. Monitor by TLC or LC-MS until vanillin is consumed. Cool to room temperature, filter off inorganic salts, and wash the solids with acetone. Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure. Partition the residue between ethyl acetate and water, wash the organic layer with water and brine, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate. Purify by silica gel chromatography using hexane/ethyl acetate mixtures to afford COc1cc(C=O)ccc1OCCCCCCCCCCCO. Overall, the original recipe using K2CO3 in acetone is plausible; the optimized recommendation is to use dry acetone, slight excess bromoalcohol, and catalytic KI to improve the SN2 alkylation efficiency.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Acid-catalyzed cyclocondensation of an N-aryl trifluoroacetoacetamide hydrate with urea to form an N-aryl 6-trifluoromethyl uracil

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Optimized single-step route: 4/5; stated recipe with only urea/toluene: 2/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The transformation is chemically plausible: the trifluoromethyl ketone hydrate/beta-ketoamide precursor can cyclocondense with urea to give the uracil-2,4-dione ring. However, urea is poorly soluble in toluene and the reaction generates water, so the stated recipe is likely slow or incomplete unless run at reflux with azeotropic water removal and preferably catalytic acid. Adding p-toluenesulfonic acid and using Dean-Stark conditions makes this a much more credible single-step synthesis.

full_recipe.procedure: Charge a dry flask equipped with a condenser and Dean-Stark trap with the aryl trifluoroacetoacetamide hydrate substrate, urea, p-toluenesulfonic acid monohydrate, and toluene under nitrogen. Heat at toluene reflux, approximately 110 °C, for 12-18 h while removing water azeotropically. Monitor conversion by LC-MS or HPLC. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and filter off insoluble excess urea if present. Wash the organic phase with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate, water, and brine, then dry over sodium sulfate and concentrate. Purify the crude product by crystallization or silica gel chromatography to afford CCOC(=O)COc1ccccc1Oc1cc(-n2c(=O)cc(C(F)(F)F)[nH]c2=O)c(F)cc1Cl. If p-toluenesulfonic acid is omitted, refluxing in toluene with urea alone is not recommended and may require 24-36 h with lower conversion.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Sonogashira coupling of aryl bromide with trimethylsilylacetylene

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High priority / Rank 1 for this single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a standard Pd/Cu-catalyzed Sonogashira coupling replacing an aryl bromide with a trimethylsilyl-ethynyl group. The substrate is complex but compatible: aryl bromide, indole NH, lactam/ketone, and tertiary amine motifs should generally tolerate mild Sonogashira conditions. The provided recipe is plausible, but using preformed Pd(PPh3)2Cl2 or Pd(PPh3)4 is cleaner than PdCl2 plus free PPh3. Degassing and an inert atmosphere are important to suppress Glaser homocoupling of the alkyne.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, charge a dry Schlenk tube with the aryl bromide precursor, Pd(PPh3)2Cl2, CuI, and optional extra PPh3. Add dry degassed DMF followed by triethylamine. Add trimethylsilylacetylene dropwise, seal the vessel, and heat at 70 °C for about 12 h while monitoring by LC-MS or HPLC. After complete consumption of the aryl bromide, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, filter through Celite to remove metal salts, and wash the organic layer with water and brine. Dry over Na2SO4, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the trimethylsilyl-ethynyl product. If conversion is slow, increase temperature to 80 °C or add an additional 2 mol% Pd catalyst; if homocoupling is observed, improve degassing and reduce CuI loading to 5 mol%.

full_recipe.reaction_name: N-benzylation of a bicyclic lactam with an arylmethyl chloride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / Rank 2 of 3 possible approaches
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is chemically plausible: the bicyclic lactam N-H reacts with the benzylic chloride by SN2 substitution to give the N-benzyl lactam product. Cs2CO3 in MeCN is a reasonable mild base/solvent system and should be compatible with the ester and pyrazole motifs. However, the lactam nitrogen is relatively weakly nucleophilic, so the reaction may be slow or incomplete without heating or iodide activation. An optimized version should use dry MeCN, 1.5-2.0 equiv Cs2CO3, optional catalytic KI or TBAI, and heating at 60-80 °C.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry reaction flask with the arylmethyl chloride reactant, bicyclic lactam, cesium carbonate, and optional KI. Add anhydrous acetonitrile, using about 10 mL per 1 mmol of arylmethyl chloride substrate. Stir the suspension at 70 °C for 12 h and monitor by LCMS or TLC for disappearance of the benzyl chloride. After completion, cool to room temperature, filter off inorganic salts, and wash the solids with acetonitrile or ethyl acetate. Concentrate the filtrate, dilute with ethyl acetate, wash with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the N-benzylated lactam product: CCOC(=O)c1cnn(Cc2ccc(CN3CC4CC4C3=O)cc2)c1.

full_recipe.reaction_name: N-benzylation of benzimidazolinone/lactam N-H with aryl benzyl bromide

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High / recommended; likely optimal single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The proposed pathway is chemically plausible: the benzimidazolinone N-H is deprotonated by K2CO3 in polar aprotic DMF, followed by SN2 benzylation with the aryl bromomethyl ester. The benzyl bromide is activated and should react cleanly. K2CO3 is mild and compatible with the methyl ester and Cbz-protected piperidine. Main risks are incomplete conversion, minor O-alkylation, or hydrolysis if water is present; dry DMF and mild heating are recommended.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry flask with the Cbz-protected piperidinyl benzimidazolinone nucleophile, dry potassium carbonate, and dry DMF. Add methyl 4-(bromomethyl)-3-fluorobenzoate portionwise or as a DMF solution. Stir at 50 °C for about 12 h and monitor by LCMS or HPLC. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and filter off inorganic salts. Wash the organic phase with water and brine to remove DMF, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the desired N-benzylated product: COC(=O)c1ccc(Cn2c(=O)n(C3CCN(C(=O)OCc4ccccc4)C3)c3ccccc32)c(F)c1.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Grignard addition of N-benzylpiperidinylmagnesium bromide to a hindered polymethoxy aryl aldehyde

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / plausible but moisture-sensitive; recommended with optimized dry, inert conditions
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a standard 1,2-addition of an organomagnesium bromide reagent to an aromatic aldehyde, followed by ammonium chloride quench to give the secondary alcohol. The aldehyde has no strongly acidic groups and should tolerate Grignard conditions. Steric hindrance around the aldehyde may slow addition, so using a slight excess of the Grignard reagent and controlled addition in dry THF is recommended. NH4Cl is appropriate as a quench/workup reagent, not as a reaction promoter. The key risk is the quality and stability of the piperidinyl Grignard reagent, especially because it contains a tertiary amine.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol aldehyde scale, flame-dry the reaction flask under nitrogen or argon. Dissolve 1.0 equiv of 2,4-dimethoxy-3,5,6-trimethylbenzaldehyde in anhydrous THF, using about 10 mL THF per mmol aldehyde. Cool the solution to 0 °C. Add 1.2 equiv of N-benzylpiperidinylmagnesium bromide solution dropwise while maintaining the temperature at 0 °C. Stir at 0 °C for 1 hour, then allow the reaction to warm to 20–25 °C and stir for an additional 2 hours. Monitor conversion by TLC or LCMS. After completion, cool the mixture back to 0 °C and carefully quench with saturated aqueous NH4Cl. Stir until gas evolution and heat release cease. Dilute with ethyl acetate, separate the layers, extract the aqueous layer with ethyl acetate, combine the organic phases, wash with brine, dry over Na2SO4 or MgSO4, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford COc1c(C)c(C)c(OC)c(C(O)C2CCN(Cc3ccccc3)CC2)c1C. Recommended optimization: keep all glassware, solvent, and reagents rigorously dry; use freshly prepared or titrated Grignard reagent; use 1.1–1.3 equiv organomagnesium reagent to compensate for steric hindrance and reagent loss.

full_recipe.reaction_name: HATU-mediated amide coupling of aryl carboxylic acid with substituted aniline

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Rank 1: Plausible and recommended single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a direct amide bond formation between the pyrazole carboxylic acid and the substituted aniline. HATU in DMF with tertiary amine base is a standard and appropriate coupling system. The methyl ester should remain largely intact under these mild, non-aqueous conditions. The aniline is moderately deactivated but should still couple under HATU activation; mild heating may improve conversion. DIPEA is slightly preferred over triethylamine, but triethylamine is acceptable.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve methyl 4-carboxy-3-methyl-1-(4-methoxyphenyl)-1H-pyrazole-5-carboxylate in dry DMF. Add triethylamine, followed by HATU at 0–25 °C, and stir for 10–20 minutes to preactivate the acid. Add 3-(1,1-difluoropropyl)aniline and stir at 25 °C for 16 hours. If conversion is incomplete, heat to 40–50 °C for an additional 4–8 hours. After completion, dilute with ethyl acetate, wash with water, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to obtain the target amide product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Amide bond formation via phosphonium-mediated coupling of heteroaryl carboxylic acid with chiral primary amine

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Rank 2 / good but not necessarily optimal
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed pathway is chemically plausible: the heteroaryl carboxylic acid reacts with the chiral primary amine to give the target amide. PyBroP with DIPEA in dichloromethane is a valid coupling system and should activate the acid efficiently. The substrate contains sensitive heteroaryl chlorides and a chiral amine, but no obvious incompatibility is expected. However, HATU or COMU in DMF/DCM often gives cleaner, faster amide coupling for heteroaryl acids, so the given PyBroP recipe is good but not the top recommendation. Racemization risk is low to moderate and can be minimized by low-temperature addition and avoiding prolonged reaction times.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the heteroaryl carboxylic acid, 1.0 equiv, in dry dichloromethane, about 10 mL per mmol. Cool to 0 °C and add DIPEA, 3.0 equiv. Add PyBroP, 1.1 equiv, portionwise and stir for 10 to 20 minutes at 0 °C to preactivate the acid. Add a solution of the chiral primary amine, 1.05 equiv, in a small amount of dichloromethane dropwise at 0 °C. Allow the reaction to warm to 20 to 25 °C and stir for 4 to 16 hours, monitoring by LCMS or HPLC. After completion, dilute with dichloromethane, wash successively with water, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine. Dry the organic layer over sodium sulfate, filter, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the target amide. Recommended optimization if conversion is poor: use HATU, 1.1 equiv, with DIPEA, 3.0 equiv, in DMF/DCM at 0 to 25 °C.

recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The starting material contains an acylatable ring NH, and the product corresponds to selective N-benzoylation with 2,6-difluorobenzoyl chloride. Triethylamine can trap HCl, so the proposed pathway is chemically plausible. However, this NH is relatively weakly nucleophilic because it is embedded in a urea/lactam system, so adding catalytic DMAP and using dry conditions improves rate and conversion. Cool the solution to 0 °C.
Add triethylamine, 2.0 equiv, followed by catalytic DMAP, 0.1 equiv.
Add 2,6-difluorobenzoyl chloride, 1.15 equiv, dropwise at 0 °C over 10–20 minutes.

Quench cautiously with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride or water at 0–10 °C.
Separate the organic phase, wash with dilute aqueous NaHCO3, water, and brine.
Dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Knoevenagel condensation of substituted benzaldehyde with thiazolidine-2,4-dione

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Rank 1 / Recommended
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed pathway is chemically plausible and appropriate: the aryl aldehyde reacts with thiazolidine-2,4-dione through a piperidine/acetic acid-catalyzed Knoevenagel condensation to form the benzylidene thiazolidinedione product. Toluene reflux with water removal is suitable and helps drive conversion. Mild buffered base is preferred to avoid side reactions at the sulfone-containing benzylic center. Use slight excess thiazolidinedione and catalytic piperidine/acetic acid.

procedure: Charge a dry flask with the substituted aryl aldehyde, thiazolidine-2,4-dione, and dry toluene at approximately 0.1 M concentration.
Add piperidine followed by acetic acid to form a mild piperidinium acetate catalytic system.
Heat at reflux, approximately 110 °C, for about 6 hours. Use a Dean-Stark trap or molecular sieves if available to remove water and improve conversion.
Monitor reaction progress by TLC, LC-MS, or HPLC until the aldehyde is consumed.
Cool to room temperature. If product precipitates, collect by filtration and wash with cold toluene or ethanol.
If no precipitation occurs, concentrate the reaction mixture and purify by recrystallization or silica chromatography using a suitable ethyl acetate/hexanes or dichloromethane/methanol system.
Expected transformation is single-step Knoevenagel condensation giving the arylidene thiazolidinedione product: CCc1ccc(C(COc2ccc(C=C3SC(=O)NC3=O)cc2)S(C)(=O)=O)nc1.

recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The submitted reactants, ethyl 3-bromo-2-oxobutanoate plus aniline with sodium bicarbonate in ethanol, are not sufficient to form the target imidazole. full_recipe.reaction_name: Amide bond formation via carboxylic acid–amine coupling

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended with optimization; original recipe is plausible but incomplete/suboptimal
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is a direct single-step amide coupling between the carboxylic acid reactant and the primary amine reactant to give the target amide. EDC.HCl/HOBt in DMF is a chemically plausible coupling system. However, the given conditions omit a tertiary amine base, which is usually required to neutralize HCl from EDC.HCl, keep the amine nucleophilic, and improve conversion. Adding DIPEA or NMM is strongly recommended. For higher reliability, HATU/DIPEA in DMF or DMF/DCM is often superior, but EDC.HCl/HOBt/DIPEA is acceptable.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or dry air, dissolve the carboxylic acid reactant, 1.0 equiv, in dry DMF at approximately 0.2 M concentration. Add HOBt, 0.5 equiv, followed by EDC.HCl, 1.3 equiv, at 0–25 °C and stir for 10–20 min to preactivate the acid. Add the primary amine reactant, 1.1 equiv, followed by DIPEA, 2.5 equiv. Stir at 25 °C for 12–18 h and monitor by LCMS or HPLC. After completion, dilute with ethyl acetate or DCM, wash with water, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the target amide product. If conversion is poor, use HATU, 1.1 equiv, and DIPEA, 3.0 equiv, in DMF at 25 °C as the preferred alternative single-step coupling protocol.

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High plausibility / recommended with minor optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The pathway is chemically plausible: the mercaptopyrimidinone reactant can be deprotonated by potassium carbonate to give a sulfur-centered nucleophile, which undergoes SN2 benzylation with the trichlorobenzyl bromide to form the desired thioether. full_recipe.reaction_name: Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling of aryl bromide with N-methyl pyrazolyl pinacol boronate

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended / high plausibility; rank 1 for this single-step disconnection
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The proposed transformation is a standard Pd-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura coupling between an electron-deficient heteroaryl bromide and a heteroaryl pinacol boronate. The listed catalyst system corresponds to PdCl2/dtBPF-type ferrocene phosphine ligand with Na2CO3 in dioxane/water, which is appropriate for heteroaryl Suzuki couplings. The Boc-protected aminocyclohexyl ether and stereocenters should tolerate these conditions. Main risks are protodeboronation of the heteroaryl boronate, catalyst poisoning by azines/pyrazoles, and incomplete conversion; these can be mitigated by degassing, using 1.2-1.5 equiv boronate, 3-5 mol% Pd catalyst, and heating at 80-90 °C.

reagents.name: PdCl2(dtbpf) or in situ PdCl2/dtBPF catalyst

Degas the mixture by nitrogen sparging or freeze-pump-thaw, then seal and heat at 85 °C for about 12 h with vigorous stirring. Monitor by LCMS or HPLC. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, filter through Celite to remove inorganic salts and catalyst residues, and wash the organic phase with water and brine. Dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the coupled product: Cn1cc(-c2cc(O[C@@H]3CC[C@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)(C))C3)c3ccnn3c2)cn1. recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / recommended with optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is plausible: thioanisole is an activated ortho/para-directing arene, and succinic anhydride with AlCl3 gives the corresponding aryl 4-oxobutanoic acid after hydrolysis. The para product should predominate due to sterics. However, thioanisole strongly coordinates to AlCl3, so excess Lewis acid is required, and ortho acylation or sulfur-complexation can reduce yield. full_recipe.procedure: On a 10 mmol thioanisole scale, dry the flask and maintain an inert nitrogen atmosphere. Carefully quench the reaction onto crushed ice containing dilute HCl, maintaining cooling because the quench is exothermic. Separate the organic phase and extract the aqueous phase with dichloromethane. Combine organic layers, wash with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify by recrystallization or silica chromatography using a gradient of ethyl acetate/hexane with a small amount of acetic acid if needed. full_recipe.reaction_name: L-proline-catalyzed Knoevenagel condensation to form an exocyclic heteroarylidenyl lactone

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / Rank 2 of 3 plausible single-step options
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is chemically plausible: the lactone/β-keto ester-like substrate contains an activated methylene/enolizable position that can condense with the heteroaryl aldehyde to give the observed exocyclic alkene after dehydration. The submitted conditions using only 'Cl' in hexane/ethyl acetate are not plausible for productive N-arylation; chlorine would cause side chlorination/oxidation, while HCl alone would suppress nucleophilicity. A base and polar aprotic solvent are required. Because 2-chloropyridines are SNAr-active, Cs2CO3 or K2CO3 in dry DMF/DMSO at elevated temperature is a reasonable single-step route, with final HCl treatment to isolate the chloride salt.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Pinnick oxidation (sodium chlorite oxidation of aldehyde to carboxylic acid)

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 1 - highly recommended / optimal single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is a selective oxidation of an aldehyde to the corresponding carboxylic acid. The proposed reagent set matches a standard Pinnick oxidation: NaClO2 with phosphate buffer in tert-butanol/water, using 2-methyl-2-butene as a chlorine dioxide/HOCl scavenger. This is highly plausible for the substrate because nitro, ether, alkene-like aromatic/enone features, and tertiary centers are generally compatible under buffered mild conditions. The recipe should be optimized by treating 2-methyl-2-butene as a reagent/scavenger rather than a true solvent and by controlling pH around 4-5.

full_recipe.procedure: Dissolve the aldehyde substrate, 1.0 equiv, in tert-butanol/water, approximately 1:1 v/v, using about 10 mL total solvent per 1 mmol substrate. Cool the mixture to 0 °C. Add 2-methyl-2-butene, 5.0 equiv, followed by sodium dihydrogen phosphate, 2.0 equiv, to maintain mildly acidic buffered conditions, pH about 4-5. Add sodium chlorite, 2.0 equiv, portionwise or as an aqueous solution while keeping the temperature below 10 °C during addition. After addition, allow the reaction to warm to room temperature, about 20-25 °C, and stir for 2-6 hours while monitoring consumption of aldehyde by TLC, LCMS, or NMR. After completion, quench residual oxidant cautiously with aqueous sodium sulfite or sodium thiosulfate, acidify to pH about 2-3 if needed, and extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the organic layer with brine, dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by chromatography or crystallization to obtain the carboxylic acid product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Ambident N/O-alkylation of a 2-pyridone derivative with 2-(2,4-dichlorophenoxy)ethyl bromide

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 3/5; plausible one-step route but not optimal for a single regioisomer
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The proposed K2CO3/DMF alkylation is chemically plausible: deprotonation of the 2-pyridone gives an ambident anion that reacts by SN2 with the bromoethyl aryl ether. However, both N-alkylation and O-alkylation are expected, matching the two products shown. This recipe is acceptable if the desired output is an N/O mixture separable by chromatography, but it is not optimal if one pure regioisomer is required. Recommended optimization is dry DMF, anhydrous K2CO3, slight excess alkyl bromide, optional catalytic KI, moderate heating, and chromatographic separation.

procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, charge a dry flask with the 2-pyridone starting material, anhydrous K2CO3, and optional catalytic KI under nitrogen.
Add dry DMF, approximately 5 mL per 1 mmol substrate, followed by 2-(2,4-dichlorophenoxy)ethyl bromide.
Stir at 60 °C for 12–16 h and monitor by LC-MS or HPLC for consumption of the starting pyridone.
Cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and filter off inorganic salts.
Wash the organic phase with water and brine, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate.
Purify by silica gel chromatography to separate the N-alkylated pyridone and O-alkylated pyridine products.

Recommendation: use this route only if both regioisomers are acceptable or separable; for a single desired regioisomer, additional regioselectivity development or protecting/tautomer-control strategy would be needed.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Carboxylic acid neutralization to sodium aryl carboxylate

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended route: 5/5; original H2SO4/EtOH recipe: 1/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The stated reactant-to-product transformation is simple deprotonation of a benzoic acid to the corresponding carboxylate. Sulfuric acid in ethanol is not plausible for forming the carboxylate; it is acidic and may instead promote Fischer esterification to the ethyl ester. A mild stoichiometric base such as NaOH, NaHCO3, or Na2CO3 in EtOH/H2O is the appropriate single-step route. NaOH, 1.0–1.05 equiv, gives clean quantitative salt formation.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.00 mmol scale, dissolve the chloro(trifluoromethyl)benzoic acid in 10 mL ethanol at room temperature. Prepare an aqueous NaOH solution using 1.05 equiv NaOH in 1 mL water and add it dropwise with stirring. Stir at 25 °C for 1 hour. Confirm complete neutralization by pH 7.5–9 or disappearance of the acid form if analytical monitoring is used. Remove solvent under reduced pressure or lyophilize to obtain the sodium carboxylate salt corresponding to O=C([O-])c1cc(Cl)ccc1C(F)(F)F. Avoid H2SO4/EtOH because it is counterproductive for carboxylate formation and may cause esterification.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Hydrogenolytic O-benzyl deprotection to give aryl 2-hydroxyethyl ether

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended with modification; ranked 1st among practical single-step options
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a standard debenzylation of a terminal benzyl ether to the corresponding alcohol. Pd(OH)2/C in methanol is appropriate, but the original recipe is incomplete because no hydrogen source is specified. If 'CO' is methanol SMILES, the solvent is acceptable; if interpreted as carbon monoxide, it would poison Pd and should not be used. Best optimized route is catalytic Pd(OH)2/C or Pd/C under H2 at room temperature. Acidic Lewis-acid deprotections such as BCl3 or TMSI are less preferred due to the basic heteroaryl/aminotriazine functionality.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.00 mmol scale, dissolve the benzyl-protected precursor in methanol, using THF as cosolvent if needed for solubility. Add Pd(OH)2/C under nitrogen. Replace the atmosphere with hydrogen by three vacuum/H2 cycles or by repeated balloon purge, then stir at 25 °C under 1 atm H2 for about 6 h. Monitor by LC-MS or HPLC until disappearance of starting material. Filter carefully through Celite to remove catalyst, washing with methanol/THF. Concentrate under reduced pressure. full_recipe.reaction_name: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) / amination of chloro-heteroaryl pyrimidine

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good and plausible pathway; recommended with optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The electron-deficient chloro-fused pyrimidine/quinazoline-like substrate is well suited for SNAr with the chiral benzylic amine. Triethylamine in ethanol is plausible because it traps HCl and keeps the amine nucleophilic. The current recipe is incomplete but chemically reasonable. Heating to ethanol reflux and using a slight excess of amine plus 2–3 equivalents of base should improve conversion. Stereochemical integrity at the benzylic chiral center should generally be retained under these mild basic conditions.

full_recipe.procedure: Charge a dry reaction flask with the chloro-fused pyrimidine substrate, 1.0 equiv, and ethanol, approximately 10 mL per mmol. Add (1S)-1-(4-chlorophenyl)ethylamine, 1.1 equiv, followed by triethylamine, 2.5 equiv. Heat the mixture at ethanol reflux, about 78 °C, for 8–16 h while monitoring by LCMS or HPLC until the aryl chloride is consumed. Cool to room temperature, remove ethanol under reduced pressure, dilute with ethyl acetate, and wash with water and brine. Dry the organic layer over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford C[C@@H](Nc1ncnc2c1CN(Cc1ccccc1)CC2)c1ccc(Cl)cc1. If conversion is low, switch solvent to isopropanol or n-butanol and heat at 85–110 °C, or use DIPEA instead of triethylamine.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Finkelstein halide exchange: primary alkyl chloride to primary alkyl iodide

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Rank 1 - recommended single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed conversion of O=C1OCCC1SCCCCl to O=C1OCCC1SCCCI using NaI in acetone is chemically plausible and appropriate. The substrate contains a primary alkyl chloride, which should undergo SN2 iodide displacement. Acetone is a good solvent because NaI is soluble while NaCl precipitates, driving the halide exchange. The lactone and thioether should generally tolerate these neutral conditions, though prolonged heating or moisture should be avoided to prevent lactone hydrolysis or product degradation.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or dry air, dissolve the chloropropyl thio-lactone substrate in anhydrous acetone at about 0.1 M concentration. Add sodium iodide, preferably 3.0 equivalents, and stir the suspension at acetone reflux, approximately 56 °C, for 12-24 hours while protecting the reaction from strong light. Monitor conversion by TLC, LC-MS, or NMR. After completion, cool to room temperature and filter off the precipitated NaCl and excess inorganic salts. Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure at low temperature. Dilute the residue with ethyl acetate or dichloromethane, wash with water and then brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify rapidly by short silica plug or column chromatography if necessary, avoiding prolonged exposure to heat or light. The optimized single-step retrosynthesis is product O=C1OCCC1SCCCI from precursor O=C1OCCC1SCCCCl via NaI-mediated Finkelstein substitution in dry acetone.

full_recipe.reaction_name: N-acylation of substituted piperidine with 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzoyl chloride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High / recommended
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed pathway is chemically plausible and likely efficient: the secondary piperidine nitrogen is acylated by the activated acid chloride to form the target benzamide. The stereocenters are not involved in bond-breaking steps, so stereochemistry should be retained. Triethylamine scavenges HCl, and dichloromethane is an appropriate solvent. Recommended optimization is slow acid chloride addition at 0 °C followed by warming to room temperature to minimize over-acylation, salt formation, or side reactions.

procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the substituted secondary piperidine amine, 1.00 equiv, in dry dichloromethane, about 10 mL per mmol, and cool the solution to 0 °C.
Add triethylamine, 2.00 equiv, dropwise or in one portion while maintaining 0 °C.
Prepare a solution of 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzoyl chloride, 1.05 equiv, in a small amount of dry dichloromethane and add it dropwise over about 30 minutes at 0 °C.
Allow the reaction mixture to warm to 20 °C and stir for about 3 hours, monitoring by TLC, LC-MS, or HPLC for consumption of the amine.
Quench carefully with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate or water, separate the organic layer, and wash successively with dilute aqueous acid, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine.
Dry the organic layer over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the desired N-benzoylated piperidine product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: SN2 N-alkylation of ethanolamine with 3-nitrobenzyl bromide to give 2-[(3-nitrobenzyl)amino]ethanol

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended with optimization; Rank 1 for this single-step retrosynthesis, original recipe Rank 2 due to unspecified stoichiometry and overalkylation risk
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The pathway is chemically plausible: ethanolamine attacks the benzylic bromide by SN2, and K2CO3 in MeCN can neutralize HBr. The main risks are bis-benzylation of the secondary amine product and minor O-alkylation. Use excess ethanolamine, slow addition of benzyl bromide or dilute conditions, and mild temperature to favor mono-N-alkylation. This is still the most direct single-step route from the given starting materials.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, add 3-nitrobenzyl bromide and dry acetonitrile to a dry flask under nitrogen or air if moisture is excluded. Add powdered K2CO3, then add ethanolamine dropwise. Stir at 40 °C for about 6 h and monitor by TLC or LC-MS until the benzyl bromide is consumed. Cool, filter off inorganic salts, and wash the solids with acetonitrile. Concentrate the filtrate. For purification, perform acid-base workup: dissolve residue in dilute aqueous HCl, wash with EtOAc to remove neutral/byproduct material, basify the aqueous layer to pH 10-11, then extract the product with CH2Cl2/MeOH or EtOAc/i-PrOH. full_recipe.reaction_name: TBAF-mediated tert-butyldimethylsilyl ether deprotection to primary alcohol

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: 1: Recommended / optimal single-step route
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is a standard fluoride-mediated cleavage of a tert-butyldimethylsilyl ether to the corresponding alcohol. Stir at 25 °C for about 2 hours and monitor by LCMS or TLC until complete consumption of starting material. Quench with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride, dilute with ethyl acetate, separate the layers, and extract the aqueous layer with ethyl acetate. Wash the combined organic layers with brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to obtain the free alcohol product: COc1ccc([C@@H](CO)Nc2ncnc3c2CN(c2ccc(C)cn2)CC3)cn1.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Modified Pfitzinger quinoline synthesis to dichloro-2-(trifluoromethyl)quinoline-4-carboxylic acids

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: B / Rank 2 of 3: plausible but not optimal as written
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The transformation is chemically plausible: dichloroisatins react with 1,1,1-trifluoroacetone under basic aqueous conditions to give 2-CF3 quinoline-4-carboxylic acids via a Pfitzinger-type ring opening/condensation/cyclization. However, the original recipe is not optimal because NaOH, AcOH, and KOAc together partially neutralize each other, and using both isatin regioisomers in one pot gives a difficult product mixture. Best recommendation: run each dichloroisatin regioisomer separately, use aqueous NaOH with an EtOH co-solvent, add excess volatile trifluoroacetone, then acidify only after completion.

full_recipe.procedure: For each dichloroisatin regioisomer, run a separate reaction. Charge the selected dichloroisatin, water, ethanol, and NaOH. After completion, cool to room temperature and acidify slowly with acetic acid to pH 2-3. Stir 0.5-1 h, collect the precipitated quinoline-4-carboxylic acid by filtration, wash with water, and dry. If both isatin regioisomers are reacted together, expect a mixture of the two regioisomeric products and more difficult purification.

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / plausible; recommended with minor optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is a nucleophilic aromatic substitution: deprotonated methoxy-2-pyridone reacts with an aryl fluoride activated by a para-nitro group. K2CO3 in dry DMF is a reasonable base/solvent system. Heating is required. Main risks are incomplete conversion and competing O-arylation of the pyridone, but the desired N-arylated product is plausible. Use dry conditions, slight excess aryl fluoride, and 2 equivalents K2CO3 at 90 °C.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry reaction flask with methoxy-2(1H)-pyridone, 2-fluoro-5-nitrotoluene, and anhydrous potassium carbonate. Add dry DMF at approximately 5 mL per mmol of pyridone. Stir the mixture at 90 °C for 12–18 hours and monitor by LCMS or TLC. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and filter off inorganic salts. Wash the organic phase with water and brine to remove DMF, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or trituration/recrystallization as appropriate to obtain COc1cccn(-c2ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc2C)c1=O.

patent_details: 31.2 g 2-Cyano-3-(4-nitro-phenyl)-acrylic acid ethyl ester (Intermediate 17.1; 126.7 mmol, 1 eq.) were suspended in a solution of 12.67 g ammonium acetate (165 mmol, 1.3 eq.) in 1270 ml ethanol and treated at room temperature with 14.08 ml of 2-oxo-propionic acid ethyl ester (126.7 mmol. 1 eq.). The resulting mixture was refluxed for 2 h and stirred at rt overnight. The precipitate was filtered off, washed with ice-cold EtOH and dried to yield 11 g of the target pyridone (35 mmol, 28% yield).   ¹H-NMR (d₆-DMSO; 300 MHz): 8.29 (d, 2H); 7.76 (d, 2H); 6.67 (s, 1H); 4.21 (q, 2H); 1.25 (t, 3H).

full_recipe.reaction_name: Piperidine-catalyzed Guareschi-Thorpe-type condensation to a 2-pyridone nicotinate

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good / plausible, but needs optimized reflux conditions
recommendation_and_ranking.rational: The proposed pathway is chemically plausible: ethyl 4-(4-nitrophenyl)-2,4-dioxobutanoate can condense with cyanoacetamide under basic amine catalysis to form the substituted 2-pyridone. Piperidine in ethanol is a reasonable base/solvent system. The main optimization is to use refluxing ethanol, slight excess cyanoacetamide, catalytic-to-substoichiometric piperidine, and an acidic workup to favor isolation of the neutral lactam product.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, charge a dry flask with ethyl 4-(4-nitrophenyl)-2,4-dioxobutanoate, cyanoacetamide, and ethanol. Add piperidine slowly with stirring. Heat the mixture at ethanol reflux, approximately 78 °C, for 6 h, monitoring by TLC or LC-MS. After completion, cool to room temperature, then to 0-5 °C. Add acetic acid dropwise to neutralize the base and promote precipitation of the 2-pyridone product. Stir for 30 min, filter the solid, wash with cold ethanol and water, and dry under vacuum. If needed, purify by recrystallization from ethanol or ethanol/DMF.

patent_details: To a solution of N-{3-[(cis)-4-hydroxycyclohexyl]phenyl}-2-(4-hydroxy-3-methoxyphenyl)acetamide (1.0 g) and triethylamine (1.6 ml) in tetrahydrofuran (14 ml) was added cyclohexanecarbonyl chloride (1.1 ml). After stirring the mixture at room temperature for 4 days, water was added to the reaction solution, the mixture was extracted with chloroform, and the obtained organic layer was washed with water and saturated saline solution. It was dried over sodium sulfate, filtered, and concentrated under reduced pressure, the obtained residue was purified by silica gel column chromatography (eluting solution; hexane:ethyl acetate), and the obtained solid was washed with hexane to afford Reference Example 11 (1.05 g).   LC-MS, m/z; 576.39 (M+H)⁺ ESI, Rt; 1.436 (min)

full_recipe.reaction_name: Double O-acylation of phenol/secondary alcohol with cyclohexanecarbonyl chloride

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Good but optimized conditions recommended; original recipe ranked 3/5, optimized recipe ranked 4/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed transformation is chemically plausible: both the phenolic OH and secondary cyclohexanol OH can be acylated by cyclohexanecarbonyl chloride in the presence of triethylamine. The amide, anisole, and stereocenters should remain intact. However, the original recipe may be slower or incomplete because the secondary alcohol is sterically hindered and phenols can require activation. Adding catalytic DMAP and using a slight excess of acid chloride improves conversion to the desired diester and reduces mono-acylated intermediates.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the phenol/secondary alcohol starting material in dry dichloromethane at approximately 10 mL per mmol substrate. Cool to 0 °C. Add triethylamine followed by catalytic DMAP. Add cyclohexanecarbonyl chloride dropwise at 0 °C over about 0.5 h. Allow the reaction mixture to warm to room temperature, approximately 22 °C, and stir for 12 h. Monitor by LC-MS or TLC for disappearance of starting material and mono-acylated intermediates. Quench cautiously with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride or water at 0–22 °C, separate the organic phase, wash with dilute aqueous acid to remove amines, then saturated sodium bicarbonate and brine. Dry over sodium sulfate, filter, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography to afford the bis-cyclohexanecarboxylate product.

patent_details: 1-Fluoro-2-methyl-4-nitrobenzene (1.32 g, 8.49 mmol) was added to a suspension of 6-chloropyridin-3-ol (1 g, 7.72 mmol) and potassium carbonate (2.13 g, 15.44 mmol) in N,N-dimethylformamide (20 mL). The reactants were reacted at 70°C. for 16 hours, then cooled to room temperature, poured into water (100 mL), and extracted with ethyl acetate (50 mL×3). The organic phases were combined, washed with saturated brine (100 mL), dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filtered, and concentrated. The residue obtained was isolated and purified by silica gel column to give 1.86 g of yellow oil in 91% yield.

full_recipe.reaction_name: SNAr aryl etherification of activated aryl fluoride with 5-chloropyridin-2-ol

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High priority / Rank 1: plausible and recommended after minor optimization
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The aryl fluoride is strongly activated toward nucleophilic aromatic substitution by a para-nitro group. K2CO3 in DMF can deprotonate 5-chloropyridin-2-ol to the pyridoxide/phenoxide nucleophile, enabling C-O bond formation. The chloro substituent on the pyridine is less reactive than the nitro-activated aryl fluoride, so selective substitution of F is expected. Main risks are incomplete conversion due to steric ortho-methyl substitution and possible O/N-arylation tautomer issues of hydroxypyridine; using dry DMF, slight excess hydroxypyridine, and 85-95 °C improves reliability.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, charge a dry flask with 1-fluoro-2-methyl-4-nitrobenzene, 5-chloropyridin-2-ol, and finely powdered anhydrous K2CO3. Add dry DMF at approximately 8 mL per 1 mmol of aryl fluoride. Stir under nitrogen at 90 °C for 16 h and monitor by LCMS or TLC. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and filter off inorganic salts. Wash the organic phase with water and brine to remove DMF, dry over Na2SO4, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography to obtain Cc1cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1Oc1ccc(Cl)nc1. If conversion is low, increase temperature to 100 °C or replace K2CO3 with Cs2CO3 at 1.5 equivalents.

patent_details: A 117 mg (0.50 mmol) portion of the mixture of 2-(8-cyano-7-methyl-5-oxo-6-phenyl-1,5-dihydro-[1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyridin-2-yl)-2-methylpropionic acid ethyl ester and 2-(8-cyano-7-methyl-5-oxo-6-phenyl-1,5-dihydro-[1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyridin-2-yl)-2-methylpropionic acid methyl ester (I-106) was heated under reflux for 3 hours in phosphoryl chloride (5 ml). After cooling, phosphoryl chloride was evaporated under a reduced pressure, and the thus obtained residue was mixed with ice water and extracted with chloroform. The organic layer was washed with brine and dried over magnesium sulfate, and then the solvent was evaporated. The thus obtained residue was applied to a silica gel column chromatography and eluted with n-hexane-ethyl acetate (9:1 v/v) to obtain 87 mg of the title compound as colorless crystals (91 mg of a mixture of the title compound and ethyl ester thereof (I-123-1) was also obtained).   MS (FAB)m/z: 369 (M+1)⁺.¹H-NMR (CDCl₃)δ: 1.78 (6H, s), 2.42 (3H, s), 3.72 (3H, s), 7.21-7.24 (2H, m), 7.51-7.57 (3H, m).

full_recipe.reaction_name: One-pot alpha,alpha-dimethylation of a heteroaryl methyl acetate by ester enolate methylation

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: Recommended modified route: 4/5; original NaH/MeI/DMF recipe: 3/5
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The disconnection is plausible: the product can arise from double alpha-methylation of COC(=O)CH2-heteroaryl using methyl iodide and strong base. However, the original NaH/DMF/MeI conditions are not optimal because NaH/DMF can be hazardous, the second alkylation needs excess base and MeI, and the electron-poor N-heteroaryl chloride/cyano system may be base-sensitive. A safer and cleaner single-step option is NaHMDS in anhydrous THF at low temperature followed by MeI, then warming to room temperature.

procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve the starting methyl heteroarylacetate, 1.0 equiv, in anhydrous THF, 10 mL per 1 mmol substrate, and cool to -78 °C.
Add NaHMDS solution, 2.4 equiv, dropwise while maintaining -78 °C. Stir for 30-60 min to generate the ester enolate.
Add iodomethane, 2.6 equiv, dropwise at -78 °C.
Allow the reaction mixture to warm gradually to 25 °C and stir for about 12 h. Monitor by LC-MS or HPLC for consumption of starting material and mono-methylated intermediate.

Quench carefully at 0 °C with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride, extract with ethyl acetate, wash with brine, dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica chromatography or preparative HPLC.
If significant mono-methylated intermediate remains, add an additional 0.5 equiv NaHMDS and 0.5 equiv iodomethane and continue stirring.

patent_details: 4-Chloro-2-[2-(cyclobutyloxy)pyridin-4-yl]phenol, (Preparation 862, 20.5 mg, 0.000074 mol) was dissolved in dimethylsulphoxide (1 mL). Potassium carbonate (24.6 mg, 0.00018 mol) was added and the reaction stirred for 10 minutes at room temperature. 3-cyano-N-(2,4-dimethoxybenzyl)-4-fluoro-N-1,2,4-thiadiazol-5-ylbenzenesulfonamide, (Preparation 68, 32.2 mg, 0.000074 mol) was added and the reaction was stirred at room temperature for 15 hours under nitrogen. The reaction was partitioned between a saturated aqueous sodium chloride solution (10 mL) and ethyl acetate (10 mL), the organic layer was washed with water (30 mL). The organic extracts were dried over anhydrous magnesium sulphate, filtered and the solvent removed in vacuo to give a colourless foam (56 mg). The material was purified using an ISCO™ companion (4 g column, eluting with 100% heptane to 7:3 heptane/ethyl acetate). Fractions containing product were combined and concentrated in vacuo to obtain the title compound as a colourless oil (45 mg). full_recipe.reaction_name: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) aryl ether formation from activated aryl fluoride and phenol

recommendation_and_ranking.ranking: High plausibility / Rank 1 for single-step disconnection
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The proposed pathway is chemically sound: the aryl fluoride is activated toward SNAr by electron-withdrawing cyano and sulfonamide substituents, and the phenol can be converted in situ to the phenoxide using potassium carbonate. DMSO is an appropriate polar aprotic solvent for SNAr. The major optimization concern is that the phenol is sterically and electronically complex, so heating and slight excess phenol/base are recommended. If conversion is poor, Cs2CO3 in DMSO or NMP would likely improve reactivity.

solvents.name: Dimethyl sulfoxide
solvents.volume: 10 mL per 1 mmol limiting aryl fluoride

full_recipe.procedure: To a dry reaction vessel under nitrogen, add the activated aryl fluoride sulfonamide, the biaryl phenol nucleophile, and finely powdered potassium carbonate. Add anhydrous DMSO to give approximately 0.1 M concentration with respect to the aryl fluoride. Stir the mixture at room temperature for 10–15 minutes, then heat to 90 °C for 12 hours. Monitor by LCMS or HPLC for consumption of the aryl fluoride. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with water, and extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the organic layer with water and brine to remove DMSO, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the aryl ether product: COc1ccc(CN(c2ncns2)S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(Oc3ccc(Cl)cc3-c3ccnc(OC4CCC4)c3)c(C#N)c2)c(OC)c1.
